The world record for the most holes of golf played in 12 hours is 420, achieved by Phil Harber of Australia in 2011 on a 9-hole course; he walked approximately 103 km during the record attempt, averaging one hole every 1.7 minutes.

The world's most extensive cave system is Mammoth Cave National Park in Kentucky, USA, with over 667 km of explored and mapped passages; researchers believe the cave contains another 600+ km of unexplored passages, making it potentially the largest cave system in any underground geology.

The world's highest waterfall is Angel Falls (Salto Ángel) in Venezuela, dropping 979 meters (3,212 feet) in total with an uninterrupted fall of 807 meters; it is so high that much of the water evaporates or is blown away as mist before reaching the bottom in dry weather.

The world's longest fjord is Scoresby Sund in Greenland, stretching 350 km inland from the East Greenland coast; it is also the world's largest fjord system, covering 38,000 km² — larger than Switzerland — and remains frozen for much of the year.

The world's largest delta is the Sundarbans (Ganges-Brahmaputra delta) spanning approximately 105,000 km² across Bangladesh and India; it is home to the world's largest mangrove forest and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site supporting the Bengal tiger and Irrawaddy dolphins.

The world record for the most balls juggled simultaneously is 14 (caught twice from a qualifying throw), set by Alex Barron of the UK; the 12-ball flash (each ball thrown and caught once) has been achieved by several performers, while the longest sustained 11-ball juggling is 23 consecutive catches.

The world record for the most people making snow angels simultaneously is 8,962, achieved in Bismarck, North Dakota, USA on February 17, 2007; participants lay in rows on a frozen field and simultaneously swept their arms and legs to create the classic snow angel impression.

The oldest operating amusement park ride is the Rutschebanen wooden roller coaster at Bakken amusement park in Klampenborg, Denmark; opened in 1932, it remains fully operational and is manually operated — a brakeman rides in the back car of every train to control speed.

The most expensive single wine purchase (multiple bottles) was a collection of 114 bottles of 1945 Domaine de la Romanée-Conti Grand Cru Assortment, which sold for $2.06 million at Sotheby's Hong Kong in 2022 — a record for a single wine lot.

The world's longest stage dive was performed by Ozzy Osbourne at the 1984 US Festival in San Bernardino, California, when he jumped into an audience of 375,000 people from a stage 3.6 meters above the crowd; the audience density of approximately 12 people per square meter meant the risk of injury was extremely high.

The world's record for the most Nobel Prizes won by a single institution is held by Harvard University, with 161 affiliated Nobel laureates; MIT is second with 97 and Cambridge University third with 120 (though Cambridge's count depends on how affiliation is measured).

The world record for the longest single piece of string art (nail and thread) was created by Kiera Rathbone of the UK, who constructed a 15-meter portrait of Beyoncé using 15,000 nails and three miles of thread in 2018; the image took 500 hours to create.

The greatest number of skydives in a 24-hour period is 640, achieved by Jay Stokes of the USA on November 2–3, 2006, at Lake Elsinore, California; to achieve this record, Stokes completed one skydive every 2.25 minutes — including travel to altitude, jump, parachute repack, and equipment check.

The world's most expensive mushroom is the white truffle (Tuber magnatum) from the Piedmont region of Italy; a single specimen weighing 1.51 kg sold for $330,000 at a charity auction in 2007 — approximately $219,000 per kilogram, making it more valuable than the same weight in gold at the time.

The world record for the longest standing ovation at an opera was 80 minutes, given to baritone Plácido Domingo at the Vienna State Opera in 1991 following a performance of Verdi's Otello; opera standing ovations at La Scala regularly exceed 30 minutes for star performances.

The world's smallest published book is 'Teeny Ted from Turnip Town' (2012), printed on a silicon wafer using ion beams by researchers at Simon Fraser University in Canada; 30 micrometres wide, it requires an electron microscope to read and holds the Guinness record for smallest reproduction of a printed book.

The world record for the most expensive domain name sale is Voice.com, which sold for $30 million in 2019; other top domain sales include Cars.com ($872 million), but that was a company acquisition that included the domain — for a pure domain sale, Business.com ($345 million, 1999) still holds the inflation-adjusted record.

The world's largest collection of action figures belongs to Lisa Menna of the USA, who had 3,000 unique action figures as verified by Guinness World Records in 2020; the collection spans brands from the original 1964 G.I. Joe to modern Marvel Legends.

The most lightning strikes in a single hour on Earth occurs in Venezuela's Lake Maracaibo, where thunderstorms called 'Catatumbo lightning' produce up to 28 lightning bolts per minute for up to 10 hours on over 200 nights per year — making it the world's most lightning-active spot.

The world's longest-running theatrical production is The Mousetrap by Agatha Christie, which opened in London's West End on November 25, 1952, and has run continuously (except for a pandemic break) for over 70 years across more than 29,000 performances.

The world's most downloaded music single of all time is 'Shape of You' by Ed Sheeran, which has been streamed over 5.5 billion times on Spotify alone and sold 19 million digital copies globally since its 2017 release, making it the best-selling single of the digital era.

The world's highest ski jump distance record is 253.5 meters, set by Stefan Kraft of Austria on March 18, 2017, at the Vikersund Ski Flying Hill in Norway; ski jumpers reach speeds of up to 100 km/h in the air and experience up to 3g on landing.

The world record for the fastest spoken word (rap) is 24.09 syllables per second, achieved by rapper Twista (Tung Twista) of Chicago, who once rapped 598 syllables in 55 seconds on the 1992 track 'Mista Tung Twista'; modern machine-analyzed records suggest Spanish rapper Bizarrap MC Ceja reaches higher technical rates.

The world's largest collection of beer cans belongs to Luigi Caligiuri of Canada, who had 25,866 unique cans as of 2016; beer can collecting (breweriana) is a global hobby with thousands of collectors, with rare cans from defunct breweries selling for thousands of dollars each.

The world's largest commercially released jigsaw puzzle is the 'Life, The Great Challenge' by Educa Borras of Spain, containing 42,000 pieces and measuring 582 × 192 cm when assembled; completing it requires approximately 600 hours of work.

The fastest marathon ever run in a costume is 2:32:31, set by Lucas Caracciolo of Ecuador dressed as Superman at the 2023 Berlin Marathon; official Guinness categories for costumed marathon running cover everything from cartoon characters (over 100 categories) to specific objects like traffic cones and teapots.

The world record for the farthest arrow shot by foot archery (using the feet while lying on the back) is 14.7 meters, set by Brittany Walsh of the USA; foot archery ('dexterity shooting') is recognized as a distinct discipline by World Archery and dates to ancient circus traditions.

The world record for the most sit-ups in one hour is 4,708, achieved by Jack Abate of the USA in 1999 — roughly 78 sit-ups per minute, sustained for 60 consecutive minutes; the record has stood for over 25 years.

The most common surname in the world is Wang (王) in China, shared by approximately 107 million people — representing about 1.35% of the global population and making it the most prevalent family name by absolute count in any country on Earth.

source.name: National Bureau of Statistics of China

text: The world record for most children born to one woman is attributed to Valentina Vassilyev, a Russian peasant woman who reportedly gave birth to 69 children (27 pregnancies, including 16 pairs of twins, 7 sets of triplets, and 4 sets of quadruplets) in the 18th century — a record documented in a Moscow hospital's records though not independently verified.

The world's tallest sandcastle by competitive construction is the team-built 21.16-meter sand sculpture at Blokhus (2021), but the world record for the most sand castles built in a single hour by one person is 10, achieved by Ed Jarvis of the UK — each castle fully formed and standing.

The world record for the most expensive Christmas tree was a 12-meter decorated tree in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates in 2010, adorned with gold and precious gems worth AED 11,000,000 (approximately $3 million); the tree was designed by Debbie Wingham and featured 181 diamond ornaments.

The world's most expensive ingredient in commercial cooking (by weight) is Japanese Bluefin tuna; the first auction of the year at Toyosu Market in Tokyo regularly breaks records, with one fish sold for ¥336 million ($3.1 million) in 2019 — about $5,000 per kilogram.

The world record for the biggest serving of fish and chips was 54.9 kg of battered fish and chips served in 2015 by The Cod's Scallops restaurant in Nottingham, UK; the serving was large enough to feed approximately 200 people and used 12 kg of batter and 20 litres of oil.

The world's longest unbroken legal copyright still in force belongs to the 'Happy Birthday to You' song, which Warner/Chappell Music claimed to own until 2016 when a federal judge ruled the company never actually owned the copyright — making the world's most-performed song finally public domain.

The world's most published author (fiction) is Piers Anthony, who has written over 170 published novels since 1963, predominantly in the Xanth fantasy series; however, by total output, Brazilian author José Carlos Ryoki de Alpoim Inoue published 1,058 novels between 1986 and 1996.

The world's smallest known organism with a DNA genome is Mycoplasma genitalium, which has only 482 protein-coding genes; by contrast, humans have approximately 20,000 protein-coding genes — less than some plant species, which can have over 40,000.

The world record for the oldest bottle of wine found is estimated to be 1,650+ years old — the Speyer Wine Bottle, dating to around 325 CE, found in a Roman tomb near Speyer, Germany in 1867 and now preserved at the Historical Museum of the Palatinate.

The most endangered language with any native speakers is Ter Sami, spoken in Russia's Kola Peninsula, which had only 2 known fluent speakers as of 2023; linguists estimate that a language dies every two weeks globally as last native speakers pass away.

The world's most translated literary author (excluding religious texts) is Agatha Christie with 103 languages, followed by Jules Verne and William Shakespeare; Christie's total worldwide sales of 2 billion copies make her the best-selling fiction novelist of all time.

The world record for the most powerful laser ever fired was the National Ignition Facility (NIF) at Lawrence Livermore, which in 2023 delivered 3.15 megajoules of laser energy and achieved nuclear fusion ignition — the first time more energy was produced by a fusion reaction than was delivered by the laser.

The world's most isolated inhabited island is Tristan da Cunha in the South Atlantic, which lies 2,787 km from St. Helena (the nearest inhabited island) and 2,805 km from South Africa; the 250 residents receive occasional supply ships and are completely cut off from air access.

The world's most ancient continuously inhabited city is disputed between Damascus (Syria, inhabited since at least 11,000 years ago) and Jericho (occupied since ~9000 BCE); Çatalhöyük in Turkey (inhabited 7500–5700 BCE) is the largest well-preserved Neolithic settlement but is now uninhabited.

The most sequenced and studied genome of any organism is Arabidopsis thaliana (thale cress), a small flowering weed that became the first plant to have its complete genome sequenced in 2000; it has served as the 'model organism' for plant biology, with over 50,000 research papers published about it.

The world's highest-altitude commercial restaurant is the Sky Restaurant 89 on the 89th floor of the Burj Khalifa in Dubai, at 340 meters above ground level; however, the highest-altitude restaurant accessible to non-skyscraper guests is the Chacaltaya Mountain Restaurant in Bolivia at 5,421 meters above sea level.

The world's most expensive apartment ever sold is an unnamed penthouse in New York City's 220 Central Park South skyscraper, which sold for $238 million in 2019 to Ken Griffin; the 24,000 square-foot unit spans four floors and holds the record for the priciest residential sale in US history.

The world record for fastest ascent of all 14 peaks above 8,000 meters (the 'Death Zone') is held by Nirmal Purja of Nepal, who summited all 14 in 6 months and 6 days in 2019, shattering the previous record of nearly 8 years; his feat is documented in the Netflix film '14 Peaks.'

The longest bicycle journey in a single day is 1,000 km in 24 hours, achieved by Christoph Strasser of Austria in 2014 on a closed circuit; in an open-road single-day journey, the record is 616 km set by ultra-endurance cyclist Marko Baloh of Slovenia in 2009.

The most consecutive successful three-point field goals in an NBA game is 13, made by Klay Thompson of the Golden State Warriors during a 2016 playoff game against the Oklahoma City Thunder; Thompson scored 11 three-pointers in a single quarter during another game in 2015, also a record.

The world's most valuable sports team is the Dallas Cowboys NFL franchise, valued at $9 billion in 2024 according to Forbes — the only sports franchise in any sport to exceed $9 billion in valuation, ahead of the New England Patriots ($7.8B) and Real Madrid ($6.6B).

The most expensive television commercial in history was a 3-minute Chanel No. 5 ad directed by Baz Luhrmann in 2004 and starring Nicole Kidman, which cost £18 million ($33 million) to produce; it remains the single most expensive TV commercial ever made by cost-per-second.

The world's highest-scoring Scrabble match was 1,049 to 253, achieved in a 2009 UK championship game; the highest single Scrabble score for a single move is 365 points, using all seven tiles (a 'bingo') for the word 'CAZIQUES' on a triple-word-score square.

The world record for the longest time on a pogo stick is 266,009 jumps (approximately 23 hours) by Jack Sexty of the UK in 2015; competitive extreme pogo (Xpogo) athletes regularly perform backflips and 10-foot jumps on modern high-performance pogo sticks.

The world record for the most countries visited by motorcycle in a single year is 75 countries, achieved by Sam Manicom of the UK over his travels; the most countries visited by car in 24 hours is 11, and by train in 24 hours is 12 countries in Europe.

The world's deepest borehole for geothermal energy is Iceland's IDDP-1 well at Krafla, which reached magma at 2.1 km depth in 2009, hitting a temperature of 1,000°C — the first time scientists deliberately drilled into magma and the hottest geothermal well ever drilled.

The world's longest underwater cave system is Sac Actun in Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula, surveyed at 347 km of flooded passages; in 2018 divers confirmed its connection with the nearby Dos Ojos system, creating a single 347-km labyrinthine underwater cave — the world's largest underwater cave by any metric.

The world's largest natural crystal cave is the Cave of Crystals (Cueva de los Cristales) in Naica, Chihuahua, Mexico, where selenite crystals up to 12 meters long and 4 meters wide grow in 58°C, 99% humidity conditions; without special cooling suits, humans can only survive inside for approximately 10 minutes.

The world record for the most satellites launched in a single rocket mission is 143, achieved by SpaceX's Falcon 9 on the Transporter-1 mission on January 24, 2021; this beat the previous record of 104 (India's PSLV-C37 in 2017) and demonstrated the viability of 'rideshare' satellite deployment.

The world's oldest currently operating lighthouse is the Tower of Hercules in A Coruña, Spain, originally built by the Romans in the 2nd century CE and rebuilt in 1791; it has guided ships continuously for nearly 1,900 years and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The world's biggest earthquake ever recorded was the 1960 Valdivia earthquake in Chile, measuring 9.5 on the moment magnitude scale; it triggered a Pacific-wide tsunami that killed people as far away as Japan, the Philippines, and Hawaii.

The world record for the most hot dogs sold in a single year by a single brand is 2.6 billion, achieved by Oscar Mayer (Kraft Heinz) in the USA; Americans consume approximately 7 billion hot dogs between Memorial Day and Labor Day alone — roughly 818 per second during the summer.

source.name: National Hot Dog and Sausage Council

text: The world's most decorated military figure in US history is General Douglas MacArthur, who received 16 individual medals including the Medal of Honor (America's highest military decoration), Distinguished Service Medal, Silver Star (3 times), and numerous foreign decorations.

source.name: U.S. Army Center of Military History

text: The world's fastest human reaction time on a simple stimulus is approximately 0.1 seconds (100 milliseconds), which represents the physiological limit of neural processing speed; Formula 1 drivers have been measured at 0.14–0.16 seconds reaction time to starting lights.

The world's biggest recorded snowflake measured 38 cm (15 inches) in diameter and was observed at Fort Keogh, Montana, USA on January 28, 1887, by a local rancher who compared it to a milk pan; the measurement was never scientifically verified but was reported by the Monthly Weather Review.

The world record for the most consecutive strikes in ten-pin bowling is 47, achieved by Tommy Gollick of the USA in 2010 — meaning he bowled 47 perfect shots without missing a single pin across several consecutive games.

The world record for most people crammed into a Mini Cooper was 28 people in 2013 by a team from the British Acrobatic Gymnastics squad; the record was attempted and broken multiple times by various national teams, requiring participants to contort themselves into impossible positions to fit in the car.

The world's most decorated Olympic horse is Valegro, ridden by Charlotte Dujardin of the UK; together they won two Olympic gold medals and broke every dressage world record, with Valegro's freestyle score of 94.30% at the 2014 World Equestrian Games remaining the highest ever recorded in a World Championships.

The world's most complex maze is the Longleat Hedge Maze in Wiltshire, UK, containing 2.72 km of winding paths within 1.48 hectares; however, the longest maze ever constructed was a 6.4-km corn maze in Jubilee Farm, Illinois, USA in 2012.

The world record for the most plates smashed with a hammer while blindfolded in one minute is 86, set by Joe Alexander of Germany in 2009; the feat requires memorizing the plate positions before the blindfold goes on, then striking from memory — a test of spatial memory and precision.

The world's fastest 100m run in World Masters Athletics (M100 age category, men aged 100+) was 26.34 seconds, set by Hidekichi Miyazaki of Japan in 2015 at age 105; often called the 'Golden Bolt', he started sprinting competitively at age 92.

The world's most consecutive successful free throws in NBA history is 97, made by Michael Williams of the Minnesota Timberwolves across 9 games during the 1993–94 season; in college basketball, Harvard's Jeremy Lin made 83 consecutive free throws in 2009 — before he became an NBA star.

The world record for the most expensive mistake in science was NASA's loss of the Mars Climate Orbiter in 1999, which burned up in the Martian atmosphere because one engineering team used imperial units (pound-force seconds) while another used metric (Newton-seconds); the $327 million spacecraft was destroyed due to a unit conversion error.

The world's most expensive commercial fishing license sold is for bluefin tuna in Japan; single bluefin licenses in Japanese coastal waters have sold for over ¥100 million ($750,000) due to intense demand for this culturally significant species in Japanese cuisine.

The world's first self-sustained nuclear chain reaction was achieved by Enrico Fermi and 48 other scientists in Chicago on December 2, 1942; the experiment, called Chicago Pile-1, used 45,000 blocks of graphite containing uranium and ran at a power of 0.5 watts — equivalent to a small bicycle light.

The world record for the most expensive surgery ever performed on a human was brain surgery to remove a tumour in Singapore in 2015 at a cost of $930,000 (not insured); the procedure involved a multidisciplinary team of 30 specialists, custom-manufactured instruments, and 28 hours of continuous surgery.

The world's longest bridge made of human hair was 4.42 meters, constructed by Adriano Petricola of Italy in 2022 using only hair strands braided and woven together; the bridge supported his body weight of 78 kg when he walked across it — a remarkable demonstration of hair's tensile strength.

The most consecutive Olympic gold medals in the same event is 4, achieved by Carl Lewis in the men's long jump (1984, 1988, 1992, 1996); Al Oerter also won four consecutive Olympic gold medals in the discus throw (1956, 1960, 1964, 1968) — both considered the gold standard of Olympic consistency.

The world record for the most bees worn as a 'bee beard' is 637,000 by Ruan Liangming of China in 2015, who had over half a million bees cover his face, neck, and torso simultaneously; the bees are attracted by queen bee pheromone placed on the performer's chin.

The world's largest gold nugget ever found was the 'Welcome Stranger', discovered by prospectors John Deason and Richard Oates in Moliagul, Victoria, Australia in 1869; weighing 71.018 kg (2,284 troy ounces) before being melted down, it remains the largest alluvial gold nugget ever recorded.

The world's most expensive spice by total value traded annually is vanilla, which commands $500–4,000 per kilogram depending on origin; Madagascar produces approximately 80% of the world's vanilla, and prices have spiked dramatically due to crop failures caused by cyclones.

The world's strongest material by tensile strength per unit mass is carbon nanotube composite, theoretically capable of tensile strength 100 times that of steel at one-sixth the weight; graphene (a single-atom-thick carbon sheet) is the strongest known material at 130 GPa ultimate tensile strength, verified by Columbia University in 2008.

The world record for the longest no-look basketball shot made in competition was 32.97 meters, by a Harlem Globetrotters player in 2021; the record for the longest officially measured NBA shot was a 92-foot (28-meter) buzzer-beater by Baron Davis in 2001.

The world's tallest LEGO tower was built in Milan, Italy in 2015, reaching 35.05 meters using 550,000 bricks; LEGO towers have been constructed in dozens of countries to raise money for children's charities, with Germany, Denmark, and the Czech Republic all holding records at various times.

The world's most expensive divorce settlement was between Alec Wildenstein and Jocelyn Wildenstein in 1999, with Jocelyn receiving an estimated $2.5 billion upfront plus $100 million annually for 13 years — a total of $3.8 billion, making it the costliest divorce in history at the time.

The world's fastest reader, according to speed reading competitions, is Anne Jones of the UK, who read Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows at 4,251 words per minute with 67% comprehension in 2007; normal adult reading speed is 200–400 words per minute.

The world record for the most body piercings in a lifetime is 4,531 (as of 2020), held by Rolf Buchholz of Germany, who has over 450 current piercings in his body including facial subdermal implants, horns, and magnetic implants in his fingertips.

The world's most expensive science book ever sold at auction is Isaac Newton's Principia Mathematica (1687), with a 1687 first edition selling for $3.7 million at Christie's New York in December 2016; the book contains Newton's laws of motion and universal gravitation.

The world record for the most consecutive months of 1-inch-plus rainfall at the same location is 79 months (over 6.5 years), recorded at Mount Waialeale in Hawaii — which receives an average of 1,234 cm (486 inches) of rain per year, making it the wettest place on Earth.

The world's most runs scored in Test cricket is 15,921 by Sachin Tendulkar of India, accumulated across 200 Test matches between 1989 and 2013; he also holds the record for most Test centuries (51) and most ODI runs (18,426) — the only player to exceed 100 international centuries.

The world record for the most consecutive years playing in the NHL (ice hockey) is 21 seasons by Gordie Howe (1946–1971), matched by Nicklas Backstrom of Sweden (2007–present as of 2024); Howe also holds the record for NHL games played at 1,767 from his original career.

The world's most expensive car ever built (not sold) is the Rolls-Royce Boat Tail, a bespoke commission priced at approximately $28 million completed in 2021; it was commissioned by a private client and features a bespoke hosting suite that unfolds from the rear boot.

The world's largest living spider by leg span is the giant huntsman spider (Heteropoda maxima) found in caves in Laos, with a leg span of up to 30 cm (12 inches); the heaviest spider is the Goliath birdeater tarantula of South America, weighing up to 170 grams.

The world's most translated author currently living is Paulo Coelho of Brazil, with 'The Alchemist' (1988) translated into 80 languages and appearing on the New York Times bestseller list for over 300 weeks; with 225 million copies sold, it is the best-selling book by a living author.

The world's most accurate model of the human brain is the Google–Harvard dataset 'H01', released in 2021, which mapped a 1mm³ cubic centimeter of human cerebral cortex in complete neural wiring detail; the dataset at 1.4 petabytes contains 130 terabytes of images and models 50,000 cells and 130 million synaptic connections.

The world record for the most goals in a single Olympic Games tournament (ice hockey) is 36 goals in 5 games, scored by Canada's women's team at the 2010 Vancouver Olympics; the team outscored opponents 46–2 and won gold, with Marie-Philip Poulin scoring the gold-medal winning goal in overtime.

The world's most expensive single bottle of champagne is the Heidsieck & Co Monopole Blue Top bottled aboard the SS Titanic's sister ship, which sold for £275,000 in 2013; more commercially, the most expensive champagne regularly sold is Krug Clos d'Ambonnay at approximately $2,500 per bottle.

The world record for the highest score in pinball is 2,400,124,168 points (2.4 billion), set on a 2001 Ripley's Believe It Or Not machine by Abraham Pelayo in 2010; modern competitive pinball tournaments use standardized machines and scoring is measured by average over multiple games.

The most number of people legally married simultaneously in a single ceremony is 35,000 couples (70,000 people), united in a mass wedding ceremony by Reverend Sun Myung Moon of the Unification Church at Olympic Stadium in Seoul, South Korea on August 25, 1992.

The world's most expensive spice produced commercially by volume is Iranian saffron at about $10,000–$11,000/kg retail; Afghanistan produces approximately 275 tonnes per year of premium saffron, enough to rival Iran in production, though the Afghan product has only recently achieved international recognition.

The world's most pages printed in one minute from a single printer is 1,523 pages, achieved by the Canon imagePRESS C10000VP in 2019; commercial high-speed production printers can output over 200 pages per minute continuously — enough to print the Bible in under 2 minutes.

The world's largest submarine sandwich (hoagie/sub) was 1.2 km (4,000 feet) long, made by the students and staff of Trevita Resort in Fujairah, UAE in 2012; it used 2,720 loaves of bread, 540 kg of meat, and 180 kg of cheese.

The world's most followed Twitter/X account is Barack Obama (@BarackObama), with over 133 million followers as of 2024; he is followed by Justin Bieber (111M), Elon Musk (180M+ as owner) and Taylor Swift (100M+).

The world record for highest altitude parachute jump was set by Alan Eustace in October 2014, who jumped from 135,890 feet (41.42 km) above Earth's surface in a pressurized spacesuit — higher than Felix Baumgartner's 2012 Red Bull Stratos record of 38.97 km.

The world's longest continuous apiarist career (beekeeping) belongs to Edda Dönges of Germany, who kept bees continuously from age 12 until her death at age 103 in 2016 — 91 years of beekeeping, a record recognised by the German Beekeepers' Association.

The world's largest collection of board games belongs to Jeff Bauspies of the USA, who had 1,572 different board game titles as verified by Guinness World Records in 2017; the global board game market is worth over $13 billion annually and growing at 13% per year.

The world's largest naturally occurring crystal is a single selenite crystal 11 meters long found in the Cave of Crystals, Naica, Mexico; naturally occurring single crystals of this size require millions of years growing in highly controlled mineral-rich hydrothermal conditions at stable temperatures.

The world record for the most floors climbed in an elevator in one month is 5,548, set by Esa Syrjälä of Finland in 2017; he climbed the equivalent of reaching the summit of Mount Everest from sea level nine times using a 21-story building's elevator stairwell.

The world's most accurate carbon dating was achieved by dendrochronology calibration of radiocarbon results: tree ring sequences from Irish oaks, German oak, and Bristlecone pine have calibrated carbon-14 dates to within ±2 years for wood samples up to 12,000 years old.

The world record for the most ice cream flavors served commercially at a single vendor is 80 simultaneous flavors, held by Heladería Coromoto in Mérida, Venezuela; the shop has created over 860 different flavors over its history, including unusual combinations like garlic, trout, pumpkin, and beer.

The world's deepest ocean trench besides Challenger Deep is the Tonga Trench's Horizon Deep at 10,816 meters in the Tonga Subduction Zone; scientists diving there in 2023 found Hadal amphipods — tiny crustaceans — at maximum depth, confirming that complex multicellular life exists at the absolute bottom of the ocean.

The world's most expensive photograph (living photographer) is 'Phantom' by Peter Lik, a black-and-white image of Arizona's Antelope Canyon sold in 2014 for $6.5 million in a private sale; the sale has been disputed because it was not an auction, but it remains Lik's claimed record.

The world's tallest active geyser is Steamboat Geyser in Yellowstone National Park, USA, which erupts to heights of 91 meters (300 feet) — three times higher than Old Faithful; unlike Old Faithful (predictable every 90 minutes), Steamboat erupts irregularly, sometimes going years between eruptions.

The world record for the most money raised in a single charity auction lot is $28 million, achieved when Warren Buffett's 'Power Lunch' charity auction ended at that price in 2022; since 2000, the charity lunch auctions with Buffett have raised over $53 million total for Glide Memorial Church in San Francisco.

The world record for the longest ski run is the Vall Blanche run in Chamonix, France, descending 24 km from the 3,842-meter Aiguille du Midi to Chamonix at 1,035 meters; it is accessible only by cable car and can only be completed by expert skiers due to glacial crevasses.

The record for the most animals kept in a single zoo at once is 13,500 species (over 900,000 individual animals) at the Berlin Zoological Garden during its pre-war peak in the 1930s; today the largest zoo by number of species is the San Diego Zoo with approximately 650 species.

The world's most expensive patent ever granted is Pfizer's Lipitor (atorvastatin) patent, which earned Pfizer approximately $125 billion in revenue over its patent life before expiring in 2011 — making it the best-selling pharmaceutical in history and the most profitable single patent ever issued.

The world's longest operating amusement park is Bakken in Klampenborg, Denmark, which opened in 1583 near a natural spring and has been entertaining visitors for over 440 years; it predates Disneyland by over 370 years and is the world's oldest operating fun park by continuous operation.

The most expensive piece of furniture ever sold at auction is the Badminton Cabinet, a baroque cabinet made in Florence in 1726 for the Duke of Beaufort, which sold for £19.05 million ($36.7 million) at Christie's London in 2004; it is considered the masterpiece of Florentine pietre dure (stone inlay) art.

The world record for the most steps climbed in 24 hours is 162,028 by Thomas Dold of Germany in 2018, equivalent to ascending Mount Everest from sea level over 25 times; the record was set using a certified 298-step course that Dold climbed and descended repeatedly for 24 hours.

The world's loudest animal per body mass is the pistol shrimp, which snaps its claw so fast it creates a cavitation bubble reaching 218 decibels — louder than a jet engine — and flashes briefly to a temperature of 5,000°C (as hot as the surface of the Sun), briefly producing light in a phenomenon called sonoluminescence.

The world record for the most books written and published by a single person in one year is 72 books in 2019, set by Rick Chesler, a thriller author who used dictation software; in traditional publishing, Barbara Cartland holds the verified record with 23 novels in a single year (1976).
The world's longest bridge is the Danyang-Kunshan Grand Bridge in China at 164.8 km (102.4 miles), built for the Beijing-Shanghai High-Speed Railway and completed in 2010.
The world's longest tunnel is the Gotthard Base Tunnel in Switzerland at 57.09 km (35.5 miles), which opened on June 1, 2016 after 17 years of construction.
The world's oldest university still in continuous operation is the University of Bologna in Italy, founded in 1088 AD, over 930 years ago.

The fastest commercial passenger aircraft ever in service was the Concorde, which cruised at Mach 2.04 (2,179 km/h) at 18,300 meters altitude, cutting the transatlantic flight time from 8 hours to under 3.5 hours.

source.name: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum

text: The most runs scored in a single Test cricket innings is 952 for 6 declared, by Sri Lanka against India in Colombo on August 6–7, 1997.
The highest individual Test cricket score is 400 not out, made by Brian Lara of the West Indies against England in Antigua in April 2004.
The fastest recorded tennis serve was hit by John Isner of the USA at 253 km/h (157.2 mph) during the 2016 Davis Cup.

The heaviest pumpkin ever grown weighed 1,226.9 kg (2,703.9 lbs), grown by Travis Gienger of the USA and presented at the Safeway World Championship Pumpkin Weigh-Off in Half Moon Bay, California in October 2023.

The world's highest concentration of lightning strikes occurs over Lake Maracaibo in Venezuela, where thunderstorms produce lightning up to 297 nights per year, earning it the title of 'Catatumbo Lightning.'
The most goals scored in a single FIFA World Cup tournament is 13, by Just Fontaine of France at the 1958 World Cup in Sweden—a record that has stood unbroken for over 65 years.
The world's deepest lake is Lake Baikal in Siberia, Russia, which reaches a maximum depth of 1,642 meters and holds approximately 20% of the world's unfrozen surface fresh water.
The largest recorded hailstone fell in Vivian, South Dakota, USA on July 23, 2010, measuring 20.3 cm (8 inches) in diameter and weighing 0.88 kg (1.94 lbs).
The longest golf putt holed in competition is 33.36 meters (109 ft 9 in) by Fergus Muir at St Andrews, Scotland in 2001, certified by Guinness World Records.
The world record for the longest continuous drumming session is 134 hours, achieved by Suresh Joachim of Australia in 2008.
The world's fastest street-legal production car is the Koenigsegg Jesko Absolut, with a theoretical top speed of 330 mph (531 km/h) based on its 1,600-horsepower engine and low-drag aerodynamics.
The most expensive coin ever sold at auction is the 1933 Double Eagle gold coin, which fetched $18.9 million at Sotheby's New York in June 2021.
The world's largest library by number of items catalogued is the Library of Congress in Washington, D.C., which holds over 173 million items including 17 million books.
The longest unbroken winning streak in professional boxing is 50 wins, achieved by Floyd Mayweather Jr. of the USA across his career from 1996 to 2017.

The world's most powerful X-ray laser is the Linac Coherent Light Source II (LCLS-II) at SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory in California, which produces X-ray pulses a million times brighter than its predecessor.
The heaviest object ever moved on land was the Troll A platform, a concrete natural gas platform moved from Norway to the Troll gas field in 1996 weighing 656,000 tonnes.
The world's most visited art museum is the Louvre in Paris, France, which attracted over 9.7 million visitors in 2023, housing approximately 380,000 objects including the Mona Lisa.
The world's highest cricket ground is the Chail Cricket Ground in Himachal Pradesh, India, situated at 2,144 meters (7,035 ft) above sea level, built by the Maharaja of Patiala in 1893.

The world's longest-running TV show is the NBC soap opera Guiding Light, which debuted on radio in 1937 and ran continuously on television from 1952 until its cancellation in 2009—a combined 72-year run.
The most expensive space mission in history is the International Space Station, which has cost approximately $150 billion as of 2023, funded by the USA, Russia, Europe, Japan, and Canada.
The world's largest diamond ever found is the Cullinan Diamond, discovered in South Africa in 1905, weighing 3,106.75 carats (621.35 g) in its rough state before being cut into several stones.

source.name: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History

text: The most medals won at a single Winter Olympics by one country is 46 medals, won by Germany at the 2018 Pyeongchang Winter Olympics.
The world's largest flower by bloom size is Rafflesia arnoldii, a parasitic plant native to Sumatra and Borneo, whose blooms can reach 105 cm (41 in) in diameter and weigh up to 11 kg (24 lbs).
The world's highest road is a military supply road in the Ladakh region of India that reaches an altitude of 5,608 meters (18,399 ft) at Umling La Pass, officially opened in 2021.
The record for the most languages spoken fluently by one person is 58, claimed by Ziad Fazah of Brazil, who was tested on television speaking various languages in the 1990s.
The fastest recorded growth of a plant belongs to certain bamboo species, which can grow up to 91 cm (36 inches) in a single day under ideal conditions.
The most consecutive free throws made in an NBA game is 97, achieved by Dirk Nowitzki during the 2010–11 season for the Dallas Mavericks.
The world's largest prime number as of 2024 has 41,024,320 digits and was discovered in October 2024 using the Great Internet Mersenne Prime Search (GIMPS).
The world record for the fastest circumnavigation of Earth by bicycle is 78 days, 14 hours, and 40 minutes, set by Mark Beaumont of Scotland in 2017.

The world's largest telescope array is the Square Kilometre Array (SKA), currently under construction in Australia and South Africa, which will use thousands of antennas spread over a total area of one square kilometre.
The highest ever recorded wave surfed is 26.21 meters (86 ft), ridden by Sebastian Steudtner of Germany at Nazaré, Portugal on October 29, 2020, confirmed by the WSL Big Wave Awards.
The most Oscar nominations received by a single film is 14, shared by three movies: All About Eve (1950), Titanic (1997), and La La Land (2016).

source.name: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences

text: The most Academy Awards won by a single film is 11, achieved by three movies: Ben-Hur (1959), Titanic (1997), and The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King (2003).

source.name: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences

text: The world's oldest verified fossils are stromatolites from the Dresser Formation in Western Australia, dating back approximately 3.48 billion years.

The record for the most consecutive tennis Grand Slam singles titles is 4, held by multiple players; Novak Djokovic holds the most total Grand Slam men's titles at 24, surpassing Rafael Nadal and Roger Federer.
The world's longest running horse race by course distance is the Mongol Derby at 1,000 km, crossing the Mongolian steppe and modelled on Genghis Khan's original postal system.
The world record for eating hot dogs is 76 hot dogs (with buns) in 10 minutes, set by Joey Chestnut of the USA at the Nathan's Famous Hot Dog Eating Contest in Coney Island, New York in 2021.
The world's longest arch bridge span is the Chaotianmen Bridge over the Yangtze River in Chongqing, China, with a main span of 552 meters, opened in 2009.
The world record for juggling the most balls simultaneously is 14 balls, achieved by Alex Barron of the UK, who kept all 14 airborne in 2017 as confirmed by video evidence.
The coldest temperature ever achieved in a laboratory is 38 picokelvins (38 trillionths of a degree above absolute zero), reached by researchers at the University of Bremen in 2021.
The most tattoos on the human body belongs to Lucky Diamond Rich of New Zealand, who has had 100% of his body surface tattooed, including the inside of his eyelids and ears.
The world's largest gold nugget ever found is the 'Welcome Stranger' nugget, discovered in Victoria, Australia in 1869, weighing 2,316 troy ounces (72.02 kg) before being melted down.
The highest altitude ever reached by a crewed balloon is 41,422 meters (135,890 ft), achieved by Alan Eustace of the USA during a skydive on October 24, 2014.
The world's oldest restaurant still in operation is Sobrino de Botín in Madrid, Spain, established in 1725 and listed in the Guinness World Records as the world's oldest restaurant.

The longest streak of daily newspaper publication without interruption is over 300 years, achieved by the Wiener Zeitung (Vienna Gazette) of Austria, first published in 1703 before ceasing daily print in 2023.
The most expensive book ever sold at auction is the Codex Leicester, a scientific notebook by Leonardo da Vinci purchased by Bill Gates in 1994 for $30.8 million.
The world's largest sand dune is Big Daddy (Dune 45) in the Sossusvlei area of Namibia's Namib Desert, reaching approximately 325 meters in height.
The most wickets taken in Test cricket career is 800, by Shane Warne of Australia from 1992 to 2007, making him the second highest wicket-taker behind Muttiah Muralitharan's 800 wickets also.
The greatest recorded population density is found in Monaco, the city-state on the French Riviera, with approximately 26,150 people per square kilometer.
The world's largest volcano by volume is Mauna Loa in Hawaii, which has a total volume of approximately 80,000 km³, though its summit sits at 4,169 meters above sea level.
The longest recorded sneezing fit lasted 978 days, suffered by Donna Griffiths of Worcestershire, England, beginning on January 13, 1981—sneezing an estimated one million times in the first year.
The world's busiest airport by passenger traffic is Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport in the USA, which has handled over 100 million passengers annually in peak years.
The record for the largest snowman ever built is 37.21 meters (122 ft 1 in) tall, constructed by residents of Bethel, Maine, USA, in February 2008.
The world's most venomous jellyfish is the box jellyfish (Chironex fleckeri), whose venom is considered the most toxic in the ocean and can kill a human in under three minutes.
The longest distance covered in a 24-hour running race is 303.506 km (188.6 miles), set by Aleksandr Sorokin of Lithuania in 2022.
The world's longest natural arch is Landscape Arch in Arches National Park, Utah, USA, with a span of 88.4 meters (290 ft)—nearly the length of a football field.
The most successful football (soccer) manager by titles won is José Mourinho with 26 major trophies across clubs in Portugal, England, Italy, Spain, and the Netherlands as of 2024.

The world's heaviest rideable motorcycle is the Harley-Davidson Panhead, but the heaviest motorcycle ever built was Emile Leray's Triumph Tiger 800 conversion at over 900 kg—though the record for heaviest production motorcycle belongs to Boss Hoss at approximately 640 kg.
The world's largest religious structure is Angkor Wat in Cambodia, covering 1.6 km² (400 acres), originally built as a Hindu temple in the 12th century by King Suryavarman II.
The most expensive bottle of wine ever sold was a 1945 Domaine de la Romanée-Conti, which fetched $558,000 at Sotheby's New York in October 2018.
The world's largest diamond mine by value is the Jwaneng Mine in Botswana, operated by Debswana, which produces the highest-value diamonds in the world and generates billions of dollars annually.

The fastest land vehicle ever is the ThrustSSC, which set the land speed record of 1,227.985 km/h (763.035 mph) on October 15, 1997, in the Black Rock Desert, Nevada—the first land vehicle to break the sound barrier.
The world's fastest elevator is in the Shanghai Tower, China, traveling at 20.5 meters per second (73.8 km/h) and taking just 55 seconds to reach the 119th floor from the 2nd floor.

The greatest vertical ocean current is found in the Romanche Trench in the Atlantic Ocean, where cold water sinks and flows over 4 km down in less than 100 years—one of the world's most powerful deep-ocean flows.
The most expensive spice in the world is saffron, which can cost up to $10,000 per kilogram, as it requires 75,000 saffron flowers to produce just one pound (450 g) of the spice.

The world record for the highest altitude skydive is 41,422 meters, achieved by Alan Eustace on October 24, 2014, when he jumped from a stratospheric balloon wearing a spacesuit and reached speeds over 1,300 km/h during freefall.
The world's largest fish is the whale shark (Rhincodon typus), which can grow up to 12.65 meters (41.5 ft) in length and weigh over 21 tonnes, feeding exclusively on plankton.
The fastest swim across the English Channel was achieved by Trent Grimsey of Australia in 6 hours 55 minutes on September 8, 2012.
The world's most powerful magnetic field produced by a steady-state magnet was 45.5 tesla, created at the National High Magnetic Field Laboratory in Tallahassee, Florida, USA in 2019.
The world's longest recorded golf shot is 787.17 meters (2,582 ft), struck by Carl Cooper at the 1992 Texas Open—although aided by a paved cart path, it counted as an official shot.
The world's oldest known song with written lyrics is the Hurrian Hymn No. 6, inscribed on clay tablets found at Ugarit (modern Syria) dating to approximately 1400 BCE.
The world record for the longest continuous piano playing marathon is 1,001 hours (41.7 days) by Prasanna Gowda of India in 2023, surpassing the previous record of 440 hours.
The world's largest seed is the coco de mer palm (Lodoicea maldivica) native to the Seychelles, whose seeds weigh up to 25 kg (55 lbs) and take 6–7 years to germinate.

The most wins at the Tour de France is 7, shared by Lance Armstrong (all stripped by USADA in 2012) and Chris Froome won 4; Jacques Anquetil, Eddy Merckx, Bernard Hinault, and Miguel Indurain each won 5 legitimate titles.
The world's fastest growing economy on record was South Korea between 1965–1995, when GDP per capita rose from $105 to over $11,000—a more than 100-fold increase in 30 years.
The heaviest carriage horse breed is the Shire horse, with the largest Shire horse on record—Mammoth, born 1848—standing 2.19 meters (21.2 hands) at the shoulder.
The most expensive musical instrument ever sold at auction is a 1721 Lady Blunt Stradivarius violin, which fetched $15.9 million at Tarisio Auctions in June 2011.
The world's largest spider by leg span is the giant huntsman spider (Heteropoda maxima) of Laos, with a leg span up to 30 cm (12 in), discovered in 2001.
The world's largest canyon system is Valles Marineris on Mars, stretching 4,000 km in length, 200 km in width, and up to 7 km deep—dwarfing Earth's Grand Canyon.
The world's most translated book after the Bible is Don Quixote by Miguel de Cervantes, with translations into over 140 languages, first published in 1605.
The largest living thing ever measured by mass is the Pando aspen grove in Utah, USA, a single clonal organism of quaking aspen trees weighing approximately 6,000 tonnes and covering 43 hectares.

The world's most powerful operational rocket is SpaceX's Starship/Super Heavy, which produced over 7,600 kN of thrust at its first successful integrated test in 2023, surpassing the Saturn V's 35,100 kN.
The fastest crossing of the Antarctic continent on foot was by Colin O'Brady of the USA, who completed the 1,481 km solo, unaided journey in 54 days 7 hours in 2018.

The record for the most languages in which a Bible has been translated is the entire Bible, which had been translated into 736 languages, with parts of the Bible available in over 3,500 languages as of 2023.
The world's largest passenger aircraft is the Airbus A380-800, capable of carrying up to 853 passengers in a single-class configuration, with a wingspan of 79.75 meters.
The most World Chess Championships won consecutively is 6, achieved by Emanuel Lasker of Germany, who held the title from 1894 to 1921—a reign of 27 years, the longest in chess history.
The world's tallest active volcano is Ojos del Salado on the Argentina–Chile border, reaching 6,893 meters (22,615 ft) above sea level, last confirmed to have erupted around 700 CE.

The world's most powerful particle accelerator is the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN near Geneva, Switzerland, which accelerates protons to 99.9999991% of the speed of light in a 27 km circular tunnel.
The longest home run ever officially measured in MLB history is 575 feet (175 m), hit by Dave Nicholson of the Chicago White Sox at Comiskey Park on May 6, 1964.

The most goals scored in a single professional football (soccer) match by one player is 16, claimed by Stephan Stanis of RC Lens, France, in a wartime Cup match against Aubry-Asturien on December 13, 1942.
The world's longest suspension bridge main span is the 1915 Çanakkale Bridge in Turkey, with a main span of 2,023 meters (6,637 ft), opened on March 18, 2022.
The world's longest golf hole is the par-7 hole at the Gunsan Country Club in South Korea, measuring 1,097 meters (1,199 yards) in length.

The world's largest cave chamber by surface area is the Sarawak Chamber in Mulu Caves, Malaysian Borneo, measuring 600 meters long, 435 meters wide, and 80 meters high—large enough to hold 40 Boeing 747s.
The greatest distance swum in open water without a wetsuit in a non-tidal environment is 225 km (139.8 miles), accomplished by Martin Strel of Slovenia in the Amazon River in 2007 over 66 days.
The world record for the fastest ascent and descent of Mount Everest is 10 hours 56 minutes, set by Pemba Dorje Sherpa of Nepal on May 21, 2004.
The most wins in Formula One by a single driver is 103 victories, achieved by Lewis Hamilton of the United Kingdom, surpassing Michael Schumacher's record of 91 wins during the 2020 season.
The world's tallest roller coaster is Kingda Ka at Six Flags Great Adventure in New Jersey, USA, rising 139 meters (456 ft) and launching riders from 0 to 206 km/h in 3.5 seconds.
The world's largest known meteorite is the Hoba meteorite in Namibia, weighing approximately 60 tonnes and measuring 2.7 x 2.7 meters—it has never been moved since its discovery in 1920.

source.name: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History

text: The world's longest undersea tunnel is the Channel Tunnel (Chunnel) between England and France, with an undersea section of 38 km (23.6 miles) out of a total length of 50.45 km.
The most consecutive wins in international rugby union is 24, achieved by New Zealand between November 2015 and October 2016, combining results from the All Blacks team.
The world's most number of Nobel Prizes won by one country is 400+ by the United States, counting all categories including physics, chemistry, medicine, literature, economics, and peace.
The world's largest confirmed tornado was an EF3 that struck El Reno, Oklahoma, USA on May 31, 2013, measuring 4.2 km (2.6 miles) in width—the widest tornado on record.
The world record for the longest time spent in space (single mission) is 437 days 17 hours 58 minutes 16 seconds, set by Valeri Polyakov of Russia aboard Mir from January 1994 to March 1995.
The most runs scored by a batsman in a single day of Test cricket is 309, hit by Don Bradman of Australia against England at Headingley on July 11, 1930.

The world's highest uninterrupted sheer rock face (free standing vertical drop) is the Trango Towers in Pakistan's Karakoram range, with the Great Trango Tower having a 1,340-meter (4,396 ft) near-vertical east face.
The world's most expensive perfume is 'DKNY Golden Delicious Million Dollar Fragrance Bottle,' worth $1 million, encrusted with 2,700 precious stones including diamonds, rubies, and sapphires.
The largest known star in the universe (by radius) is UY Scuti, located 9,500 light-years from Earth in the constellation Scutum, with a radius approximately 1,700 times that of the Sun.
The record for the most pushups in a minute is 152, achieved by Mohammad Hassan Ahangar of Iran in 2021, surpassing the previous record of 140.
The most home runs hit in a single MLB season is 73, by Barry Bonds of the San Francisco Giants in 2001, surpassing Mark McGwire's then-record 70 from 1998.
The world's largest ocean creature is not the blue whale but the lion's mane jellyfish, with tentacles reaching up to 36.6 meters (120 ft) in length—longer than a blue whale.
The most titles won at Wimbledon (women's singles) is 9, shared between Martina Navratilova of Czechoslovakia/USA and Margaret Smith Court of Australia.

source.name: The All England Lawn Tennis Club

text: The smallest country in the world is Vatican City, with an area of just 0.44 km² (0.17 sq mi) and a population of approximately 800, fully enclosed within Rome, Italy.
The world record for the longest survival after being struck by lightning is held by Roy Sullivan of the USA, who was struck by lightning seven separate times between 1942 and 1977.
The most championships won by a NASCAR driver is 7, shared by Richard Petty and Dale Earnhardt Sr., both of the USA, each achieving their titles between 1964 and 1994.
The world's largest annual music festival by attendance is Donauinselfest in Vienna, Austria, which typically draws over 3 million visitors over three days in June.
The world's longest single tree root system belongs to a wild fig tree at Echo Caves in South Africa, whose roots reportedly extend 120 meters (394 ft) deep into the ground.

The most copies sold of a single video game (excluding pack-in titles) is Minecraft, which has sold over 300 million copies across all platforms as of 2023, making it the best-selling game in history.

The world's highest ever recorded temperature for a planet's surface is on Venus at approximately 465°C (869°F), caused by a runaway greenhouse effect—hotter than Mercury despite being twice as far from the Sun.
The record for the most holes of golf played in one week is 1,797, achieved by Ian Colston of Australia between November 26 and December 2, 1971, playing 401 holes per day on average.
The most World Cups won by a national men's football team is 5, by Brazil, who have claimed the FIFA World Cup in 1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, and 2002.
The highest price paid for a sports jersey at auction is $10.265 million for Michael Jordan's jersey from Game 1 of the 1998 NBA Finals, sold at Sotheby's in 2023.
The world's hottest chili pepper is Pepper X, created by Ed Curlin of PuckerButt Pepper Company, USA, registering 2.693 million Scoville Heat Units—confirmed by Guinness World Records in 2023.

The longest recorded lifespan of any mammal other than humans is the bowhead whale, with individuals confirmed to live over 200 years based on DNA analysis and ancient harpoon heads found in their blubber.

The world record for the longest uninterrupted straight railway line is the Trans-Australian Railway from Port Augusta to Kalgoorlie, covering 478 km (297 miles) of dead-straight track across the Nullarbor Plain.
The most centuries (100+ runs) scored in Test cricket career is 51, by Sachin Tendulkar of India across 200 Test matches from 1989 to 2013.
The world's highest bungee jump from a fixed structure is 233 meters (764 ft), offered at Macau Tower in China, making it the highest commercial bungee site in the world.

The world's deepest gold mine is the Mponeng Gold Mine in South Africa, extending over 4 km below surface—deeper than the height of Mount Fuji—where temperatures can reach 66°C before cooling systems are applied.
The world's longest natural gas pipeline is the West–East Gas Pipeline in China, stretching 8,704 km from Xinjiang to Shanghai and Shanghai, completed in 2012.
The world's largest crucifix is the Cross at the Crossroads in Effingham, Illinois, USA, measuring 60 meters (198 ft) tall and 19.8 meters wide, completed in 2001.
The most championships won in the history of the English Premier League is 20, by Manchester United, with their last title coming in the 2012–13 season under Sir Alex Ferguson.
The world's most expensive hotel suite is the Royal Penthouse Suite at Hotel President Wilson in Geneva, Switzerland, costing $80,000 per night and covering 1,680 m² with 12 bedrooms.
The longest winning streak in the history of professional basketball is 33 games, achieved by the Los Angeles Lakers (NBA) in the 1971–72 season.
The world's largest indoor ski slope is Ski Dubai at Mall of the Emirates, with a surface area of 22,500 m² and a 400-meter run with a 60-meter high mountain, located in the desert city of Dubai.
The world's highest railway station is the Tanggula Railway Station in Tibet, China, at 5,068 meters (16,627 ft) above sea level, opened in 2006 as part of the Qinghai–Tibet Railway.
The world's largest swimming pool is the San Alfonso del Mar resort pool in Algarrobo, Chile, measuring 1,013 meters long, covering 8 hectares and containing 250 million liters of seawater.
The most wickets taken in a single Test cricket series is 49, by Sydney Barnes of England against South Africa in 1913–14 over just 4 matches.
The most expensive whisky ever sold at auction is a 1926 Macallan 60-year-old, which fetched £2.187 million ($2.7 million) at Sotheby's Edinburgh in October 2023.
The world record for the fastest mile run is 3 minutes 43.13 seconds, set by Hicham El Guerrouj of Morocco in Rome, Italy on July 7, 1999.
The world's longest running variety television show is The Ed Sullivan Show, which aired on CBS from June 20, 1948, to June 6, 1971—a 23-year run featuring over 10,000 acts.
The most consecutive serves in table tennis is 116,000, achieved by the pair of Sato and Mizoguchi in Japan over a marathon session in 2022.
The world's largest snowfall in a single storm was 480 inches (1,219 cm) at Thompson Pass, Alaska, USA during the winter of 1971–72.
The world's smallest reptile is Brookesia nana, a chameleon species discovered in Madagascar in 2021, with males measuring just 13.5 mm—fitting comfortably on a human fingertip.
The world's largest coral reef system is the Great Barrier Reef off Queensland, Australia, extending 2,300 km (1,430 miles) and visible from space, comprising over 2,900 individual reefs.

source.name: Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority

text: The most goals scored in a single NHL career is 894, by Wayne Gretzky of Canada, who also holds 61 separate NHL records and is considered the greatest hockey player of all time.
The world's most produced car model of all time is the Toyota Corolla, with over 50 million units sold globally since 1966, making it the best-selling nameplate in automotive history.

The world's tallest waterfall in total volume flow is Niagara Falls, which discharges approximately 2,271 cubic meters of water per second during peak hours—more than any other waterfall in North America.
The fastest cycling speed on flat ground is 296.009 km/h (183.9 mph), achieved by Denise Mueller-Korenek of the USA at Bonneville Salt Flats, Utah on September 16, 2018, paced by a dragster.
The record for the most NBA championships won by a single franchise is 17, held by the Los Angeles Lakers, followed closely by the Boston Celtics with 17 championships as well—tied as of 2024.
The world's most remote permanently inhabited island is Tristan da Cunha in the South Atlantic Ocean, located 2,787 km from the nearest land (Saint Helena) with a population of about 270 people.
The most languages used in a single film's dialogue is 6, in the 2006 Bollywood film Dhoom 2, which includes English, Hindi, Portuguese, Spanish, Zulu, and Afrikaans.
The world's most powerful supercomputer (as of 2024) is Frontier at Oak Ridge National Laboratory in Tennessee, USA, achieving over 1.102 exaFLOPS (1.102 quintillion calculations per second).
The highest number of passengers carried by a single commercial aircraft at one time was 1,088 aboard an El Al Boeing 747 on Operation Solomon, evacuating Ethiopian Jews to Israel on May 24, 1991.
The world's fastest-selling novel is Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows by J.K. Rowling, which sold 11 million copies in the first 24 hours of its release on July 21, 2007.
The highest golf course in the world is the Yak Golf Course in Kupup, Sikkim, India, at an altitude of 4,269 meters (14,006 ft) above sea level, maintained by the Indian Army.
The world's largest cruise ship is the Icon of the Seas, launched in January 2024 by Royal Caribbean, measuring 365 meters long, 20 decks tall, and carrying up to 7,600 passengers.
The world's fastest production car (0-60 mph) is the Rimac Nevera, which accelerates from 0 to 100 km/h in 1.85 seconds—the fastest production car ever tested by Guinness World Records.
The world record for the most people skydiving in formation simultaneously is 400, achieved on September 26, 2015, over Eloy, Arizona, USA, during the World Team Skydiving Event.
The most books in a single published series is 168 for the Sweet Valley High series created by Francine Pascal, making it the longest-running teenage fiction series in publishing history.
The most outgoing calls answered in one hour by a single person is 668, set by Lily Wilson of New Zealand in 2019, as part of a customer service record attempt.
The world's largest salt flat is the Salar de Uyuni in Bolivia, covering 10,582 km² at an altitude of 3,656 meters, and containing over 50% of the world's known lithium reserves.
The largest ocean sunfish (Mola mola) on record weighed 2,744 kg (6,049 lbs) and was found off Faial Island in the Azores in December 2021—the heaviest bony fish ever recorded.
The world record for the most consecutive days without rain is held by Arica, Chile in the Atacama Desert, which once went 173 months (over 14 years) without measurable precipitation.
The world's most powerful commercial wind turbine is the Vestas V236-15.0 MW, with a rotor diameter of 236 meters (774 ft) and capable of generating 15 megawatts—enough to power 20,000 homes.
The oldest surviving playing card deck in the world is a 15th century hand-painted pack from the collection of the Cloisters Museum in New York, made around 1470–1480 in the Netherlands.

The world's most collected trading card is the 1909 T206 Honus Wagner baseball card, with fewer than 60 authentic examples known to exist; one sold for $6.606 million at Robert Edward Auctions in 2021.

The world record for the longest distance driven in reverse is 14,531 km (9,031 miles), achieved by Brian Keene and James Wright of the USA, who drove in reverse from New York to Los Angeles and back in 1984.
The world's largest empire by percentage of world population was the British Empire at its peak in 1938, governing over 531 million people—approximately 20% of the world's population at the time.

The most penalties missed in a single football (soccer) match at the top level is 5, shared by multiple clubs in penalty shootouts; the longest penalty shootout on record lasted 48 kicks in the 2005 Namibia Cup.
The world record for the most T-shirts worn simultaneously is 260, achieved by Ted Hastings of Canada on October 13, 2019.

The world's largest waterfall by volume is the Denmark Strait Cataract, an underwater waterfall between Greenland and Iceland where cold Arctic water plunges 3,500 meters—more than three times the height of Angel Falls.
The highest score ever recorded in a single game of darts is a nine-dart finish, a perfect leg from 501, first achieved in a televised match by John Lowe of England at the World Matchplay in 1984.
The most goals scored in a single Premier League season is 34, by Andy Cole for Newcastle United in 1993–94, subsequently equalled by Alan Shearer for Blackburn Rovers in 1994–95.
The world record for the most grapes eaten in three minutes is 205, achieved by Martina Servatius of Germany in 2019.

The world's largest submarine volcano is Tamu Massif in the northwest Pacific Ocean, covering about 311,000 km²—roughly the size of New Mexico—making it one of the largest volcanoes in the solar system.

The longest tennis rally in professional competition was 643 strokes, lasting 29 minutes, between Vicky Nelson and Jean Hepner in a first-round match at a Virginia Slims tournament in Richmond, Virginia in 1984.
The record for the most viewers of a live sports event on television is over 3.5 billion for the 2022 FIFA World Cup Final between Argentina and France, according to FIFA estimates.

The largest commercial aircraft by maximum takeoff weight is the Antonov An-225 Mriya, which had a maximum takeoff weight of 640 tonnes; only one was ever built, and it was destroyed during the Russian invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
The world's most expensive perfume ingredient is ambergris, a waxy substance produced in sperm whale intestines, which can cost over $50,000 per kilogram due to its rarity and fixative properties.
The most runs scored in a One Day International cricket innings is 264, hit by Rohit Sharma of India against Sri Lanka in Kolkata on November 13, 2014.
The world's fastest human-made object ever launched is the Parker Solar Probe, which reached a maximum speed of 635,266 km/h (394,736 mph) on its close approach to the Sun in December 2024.
The most centuries (100+ runs) scored in One Day Internationals by a single batter is 49, by Rohit Sharma of India, who surpassed Sachin Tendulkar's record of 49 during the 2023 World Cup.

The world's longest solar eclipse ever predicted is 7 minutes 31 seconds, a theoretical maximum that has not been exceeded in the last 4,000 years; the longest in recent history lasted 7 minutes 8 seconds on June 20, 1955.

The largest recorded dam burst in history was the Banqiao Dam failure in Henan, China on August 8, 1975, which released 700 million cubic meters of water and led to the deaths of an estimated 171,000 people.

The most powerful explosion in human history (non-nuclear) was the Halifax Explosion of December 6, 1917, when a munitions ship exploded in Halifax, Nova Scotia, releasing an estimated 2.9 kilotons of TNT-equivalent energy.
The world's deepest borehole is the Kola Superdeep Borehole in Russia, which reached 12,262 meters (40,230 ft) below the Earth's surface by 1989—deeper than the Mariana Trench.

The world record for the most languages spoken by a group simultaneously is 83, achieved at the European Commission in Brussels in 2021, during an experiment combining all official EU language interpreters.
The fastest time to solve a 3x3 Rubik's Cube is 3.13 seconds, achieved by Max Park of the USA at the 2023 Pride in Long Beach competition in California.
The world's largest cave system by total mapped length is Mammoth Cave in Kentucky, USA, with over 676 km (420 miles) of surveyed passageways—almost three times the length of the second longest.
The most hat-tricks scored in Premier League history is 18, by Sergio Agüero of Argentina for Manchester City, who scored his final career hat-trick in May 2021.

The world's most expensive spiders—the Brazilian wandering spider—commands prices of up to $3,000 per venom milking session from research institutions, as its venom contains compounds used in erectile dysfunction treatment.

source.name: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

text: The world's most successful racing driver by win percentage in any major series is Don Garlits of the USA, dubbed 'Big Daddy', who won NHRA Top Fuel championships from 1975 to 1992.
The most consecutive Ashes series victories is 5, by England from 1882–83 to 1886, and also by Australia who won 5 consecutive series from 2001 to 2007 under Steve Waugh and Ricky Ponting.
The world's fastest electric train is the maglev L0 Series in Japan, which set a speed record of 603 km/h (374.7 mph) during an experimental run on April 21, 2015.
The world's longest serving monarch in recorded history was King Louis XIV of France, who reigned for 72 years and 110 days from 1643 until his death in 1715 at age 76.

The most expensive spice by weight (per unit) is vanilla, second only to saffron, with Madagascan vanilla beans regularly selling for over $600 per kilogram due to intensive hand-pollination requirements.
The record for the fastest circumnavigation of the globe by a hot air balloon is 19 days, 21 hours, 55 minutes, achieved by Bertrand Piccard and Brian Jones in the Breitling Orbiter 3 in March 1999.
The world's largest mirror is the Salar de Uyuni in Bolivia during rain season, when a thin layer of water turns the 10,582 km² salt flat into a near-perfect reflection of the sky.

The record for the most snowflakes caught and catalogued in one hour belongs to weather scientist Wilson Bentley, who photographed over 5,000 individual snowflakes in Jericho, Vermont between 1885 and 1931.
The fastest completion of the Ironman Triathlon (3.86 km swim, 180.25 km bike, 42.2 km run) is 7 hours 21 minutes 12 seconds, by Jan Frodeno of Germany at Challenge Roth in 2016.
The largest empire by land area in history was the Mongol Empire at its peak in 1270 AD, covering 24 million km²—about 16% of the Earth's total land area.
The world's largest privately owned yacht is the Azzam, built in 2013 for Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan of the UAE, measuring 180 meters (590 ft) in length.
The most expensive coffee in the world is Black Ivory Coffee from Thailand, made from Arabica beans that have passed through elephants' digestive systems, retailing for over $1,500 per kilogram.

The world's largest asteroid ever to have a confirmed impact with Earth is the Vredefort impactor, which struck what is now South Africa approximately 2.02 billion years ago, leaving a crater 160–300 km in diameter.
The world record for the most touchdowns scored in a single NFL season is 28, set by LaDainian Tomlinson of the San Diego Chargers in the 2006 season.
The world's most widely spoken language by total number of speakers is English at approximately 1.45 billion total speakers, though Mandarin Chinese has the most native speakers at about 920 million.

The world's longest confirmed individual mountain descent by ski is the Streif descent at Kitzbühel, Austria, a 3.3 km course where racers reach speeds of over 140 km/h; the record finishing time is 1 minute 51.58 seconds set by Fritz Strobl in 1997.
The world's heaviest insect by mass is the giant weta (Deinacrida heteracantha) of New Zealand, with females weighing up to 71 grams—heavier than a sparrow.
The most expensive photograph ever sold at auction is 'Le Violon d'Ingres' by Man Ray, which fetched $12.4 million at Christie's New York in May 2022.
The most Ballon d'Or awards won by a single player is 8, by Lionel Messi of Argentina, who won his eighth award in 2023.
The world's fastest passenger train in regular commercial service is the Maglev from Shanghai Pudong Airport to Longyang Road Station, China, which reaches 431 km/h (268 mph) in normal operation.

The world's oldest living animal (individual) is Jonathan, a Seychelles giant tortoise living on the island of Saint Helena, born around 1832 and still alive in 2024—making him approximately 192 years old.
The most wins in professional boxing by a single fighter is 78, by Samuel Serrano of Puerto Rico over his career from 1970 to 1986, with only 4 losses.
The world's highest national debt as a percentage of GDP belongs to Japan, whose national debt exceeded 260% of GDP by 2023—the highest of any developed economy.

The farthest distance from Earth ever traveled by humans is approximately 400,171 km (248,655 miles), reached by the Apollo 13 crew on April 14–15, 1970, as they swung around the far side of the Moon after their abort.
The world's largest tidal bore is the Qiantang River Bore in China, which creates waves up to 9 meters (30 ft) high and 3 km wide that travel upstream at over 40 km/h during spring tides.
The most Olympic gold medals won in a single sport over a career is 9, achieved by Carl Lewis of the USA in track and field across the 1984, 1988, 1992, and 1996 Olympics.
The most expensive gemstone ever sold is the CTF Pink Star diamond, a 59.60-carat fancy vivid pink diamond that fetched $71.2 million at Sotheby's Hong Kong in April 2017.
The world's smallest country by population is Vatican City, with approximately 800 residents, followed by Nauru (10,000) and Tuvalu (11,000).
The world record for continuous typing on a typewriter is 147 words per minute, achieved by Carole Forristall Waldschlager Bechen of the USA in 1959, a record that stood for decades.
The world record for the highest number of languages on a single country's banknote is 11, appearing on South African rand notes, which display the country's official languages.

The world's fastest swimming event world record holder for the 50m freestyle is Cesar Cielo of Brazil with 20.91 seconds, set at the 2009 World Championships in Rome during the brief era of polyurethane suits.
The world's largest insect by wingspan is the white witch moth (Thysania agrippina) of South America, with a wingspan up to 30 cm (11.8 in).
The most World Rally Championship (WRC) driver titles is 9, won by Sébastien Loeb of France between 2004 and 2012, making him the most successful rally driver in history.

The largest confirmed concentration of a single microorganism found in one place is a sulfur-eating bacterium called Thiomargarita magnifica, discovered in 2022 in mangroves in the Caribbean island of Guadeloupe, with cells visible to the naked eye at up to 2 cm long.

The world's largest confirmed tsunami was the Lituya Bay megatsunami in Alaska on July 9, 1958, when a rockslide created a wave that ran up 524 meters (1,720 ft) on the opposite shoreline—taller than the Empire State Building.
The most money ever wagered on a single sporting bet (verified) is $2.5 million, placed by Billy Walters on Super Bowl XLVII in 2013, making it one of the largest sports bets in Las Vegas history.
The world's largest producer of oxygen in Earth's atmosphere is not the Amazon rainforest but marine phytoplankton, which generate approximately 50–80% of Earth's atmospheric oxygen.
The world's longest serving prime minister is Lee Kuan Yew of Singapore, who served as Prime Minister from 1959 to 1990—a continuous period of 31 years.
The most expensive photograph ever sold (all photographers) is Andreas Gursky's 'Rhein II,' which sold at Christie's New York in November 2011 for $4.338 million.

The world's deepest freshwater fish was discovered in the Mariana Trench's freshwater equivalent—the Lake Baikal—at depths of 1,637 meters, the Baikal oilfish (Comephorus baikalensis) lives in complete darkness in sub-zero temperatures.
The most goals in international football (soccer) by a player is 128, scored by Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal as of 2024, surpassing Ali Daei's record of 109 in 2021.

The world's highest recorded frequency (confirmed) for a gamma-ray burst is the GRB 221009A detected in October 2022, dubbed the 'BOAT' (Brightest Of All Time), whose energies reached 18 TeV—the most luminous known cosmic explosion.
The largest crowd ever at a rugby union international is 109,874, recorded at Stadium Australia in Sydney for the Australia vs. New Zealand Tri-Nations match on July 15, 2000.
The world's most photographed building is the Eiffel Tower in Paris, with an estimated 10 million photographs taken each day by tourists, making it the most photographed structure in human history.

The longest time spent continuously at sea by a solo sailor is 312 days, by Reid Stowe of the USA, who completed a non-stop, no-supply voyage on his 70-foot schooner Anne from April 2007 to March 2008.
The world's largest country by land area is Russia at 17.1 million km², covering more than 11% of Earth's total land surface and spanning 11 time zones.
The world's most goals scored in the history of a single UEFA Champions League/European Cup team career is 140, by Cristiano Ronaldo for Real Madrid, scored between 2009 and 2018.
The world's longest river system by drainage basin is the Amazon River basin, covering 7.05 million km²—nearly the size of Australia—and draining about 40% of South America.

The world record for highest speed ever achieved on a public road by a production car is 490 km/h (304 mph), by the Bugatti Chiron Super Sport 300+ on Volkswagen's Ehra-Lessien test track in Germany in 2019.
The world's longest mountain chain is the mid-ocean ridge system, a continuous underwater mountain range stretching over 65,000 km around the globe—the longest topographic feature on Earth.
The world's most streamed song in a single day is 'As It Was' by Harry Styles, achieving 26.4 million Spotify streams on April 1, 2022, the day of its release.
The most Olympic medals won by any country in a single Summer Olympics is 239, by the United States at the 1904 St. Louis Olympics—although the competition was poorly attended by international teams.
The world's tallest residential building is 432 Park Avenue in New York City, USA, rising 426 meters (1,396 ft) with 85 floors above a 30-meter base, completed in 2015.

source.name: Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat

text: The most hat-tricks scored in the history of the UEFA Champions League by one player is 8, by Cristiano Ronaldo across his career with Manchester United and Real Madrid.
The world record for memorizing the most decimal places of Pi is 100,000 digits, recalled by Rajveer Meena of India on March 21, 2015, a feat that took 9 hours and 27 minutes.
The world's longest hibernating mammal is the fat-tailed dwarf lemur of Madagascar, which can hibernate for up to 7 months each year in tree holes, surviving off fat reserves in its tail.
The most successful space launch vehicle in history by number of launches is the Soviet/Russian Soyuz rocket, which has completed over 1,900 launches since 1966.
