The longest confirmed shot put throw in athletics history is 23.37 meters, set by Ryan Crouser of the USA at the 2023 World Athletics Championships in Budapest, Hungary.
The world's most lightning-struck place is the village of Kifuka in the Democratic Republic of Congo, which receives over 158 lightning flashes per square kilometer per year.
The world's largest confirmed crocodile in captivity is Lolong, a saltwater crocodile captured in the Philippines in 2011 measuring 6.17 meters (20 ft 3 in) and weighing 1,075 kg.
The record for the most consecutive days above 40°C (104°F) in any city is 54 days in Oodnadatta, South Australia in 2023–24, breaking all known records for sustained extreme heat.
The most Tour de France stage wins by a single rider is 34, by Eddy Merckx of Belgium, 'The Cannibal,' who won stages across seven Tour de France participations from 1969 to 1975.
The most expensive comic book ever sold is Action Comics #1 (June 1938), the first appearance of Superman, which sold for $6 million in a private sale in April 2022.
The world's largest recorded snowstorm dropped 6.3 meters (250 inches) of snow in seven days during the Sierra Nevada of California in February 1959.
The most Grand Slam tennis titles won in the Open Era by a male player is 24, by Novak Djokovic of Serbia, with his 24th coming at the 2023 US Open.
The world's greatest natural spectacle is arguably the annual migration of over 1.5 million wildebeest across the Serengeti-Mara ecosystem in Tanzania and Kenya, known as the Great Migration.

The world record for the most rotations completed by a figure skater in a single jump is 4, a quadruple jump; Nathan Chen of the USA was the first to land 6 different quads in a single free skate program in 2018.

The world's most expensive natural material by weight is antimatter, which theoretically costs about $62.5 trillion per gram to produce; even minuscule amounts require particle accelerators running for years.
The highest-altitude lake in the world navigable by large vessels is Lake Titicaca on the Peru-Bolivia border at 3,812 meters (12,507 ft) above sea level, covering 8,372 km².
The world's largest active methane seep was discovered in the Arctic Ocean near Siberia, where methane hydrates bubble up from the seafloor in an area covering over 150,000 km².
The record for the most consecutive perfect 10 scores in Olympic gymnastics history is held by Nadia Comaneci, who received seven perfect 10.0 scores at the 1976 Montreal Olympics.
The world's most expensive cocktail is the Winston Cocktail served at Club 23 in Melbourne, Australia, containing a blend of Croizet 1858 Cuvée Leonie cognac priced at $12,500 each.

The world's largest hydroelectric project under construction is the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam on the Blue Nile, which when completed will be Africa's largest power station at 6,450 megawatts capacity.
The most expensive chess set ever sold was a jewel-encrusted set made in 2010 by Charles Hollander Diamonds, valued at $600,000, featuring diamonds, rubies, emeralds, and sapphires.
The longest bone in the human body is the femur (thigh bone), accounting for approximately 26.74% of a person's height; the femur of Robert Wadlow, the tallest man ever, measured 47.36 cm.
The world's oldest known cave paintings are the animal paintings in the Chauvet Cave in the Ardèche region of France, dated to approximately 36,000 years ago.
The most expensive bottle of spirits ever sold is a 1926 Macallan Peter Blake single malt Scotch whisky, which fetched £1.5 million ($1.9 million) at Bonhams auction in 2018.
The world record for the most apples peeled in one hour is 16.47 kg by Sharpel Murjaparliev of Turkmenistan in 2014.
The most recorded sunspot activity during a single solar cycle was Cycle 19, peaking in November 1957 with a smoothed monthly sunspot number of 201.3—the most active solar cycle in modern records.
The world's longest established wildlife corridor is the Selous-Niassa Wildlife Corridor in Tanzania and Mozambique, spanning 160,000 km² and connecting two of Africa's largest game reserves.
The world's fastest roller coaster by acceleration is the do-dodonpa at Fuji-Q Highland in Japan, which accelerates from 0 to 180 km/h in just 1.56 seconds using a compressed-air launch.
The most consecutive 3-pointers made in an NBA game is 13, by Klay Thompson of the Golden State Warriors during a 52-point performance against the Chicago Bulls on October 29, 2018.
The world's largest concentration of active volcanoes is the Pacific Ring of Fire, a zone encompassing over 450 volcanoes that account for 75% of all active volcanoes on Earth.
The record for the most aircraft simultaneously airborne worldwide at any one time is approximately 13,000, recorded during peak hours in August 2018 by Flightradar24.
The world's largest collection of meteorites in a single institution is at the Antarctic Search for Meteorites (ANSMET) archive, with over 22,000 specimens recovered from Antarctica since 1976.
The most consecutive Wimbledon men's singles titles is 5, won by Björn Borg of Sweden from 1976 to 1980.

source.name: The All England Lawn Tennis Club

text: The world's largest dam by volume of material used is the Syncrude Tailings Dam in Alberta, Canada, containing 540 million cubic meters of material—the largest dam by volume on Earth.
The longest legal journey by car on a single tank of fuel was 2,837.4 km (1,763 miles), achieved by a pair of French engineers driving a Volkswagen Passat BlueMotion diesel in 2011.
The world's most expensive watch ever sold at auction is a Patek Philippe Grandmaster Chime Ref. 6300A-010, which fetched CHF 31 million ($31.19 million) at Only Watch Geneva in November 2019.
The most copies sold of a single album in one week is 3.38 million, by *NSYNC's 'No Strings Attached' in the first week of release in March 2000 in the United States.
The most expensive commercial real estate transaction in history is the sale of the GM Building in New York City for $2.8 billion in 2008 to a consortium led by Mortimer Zuckerman.
The world's highest altitude marathon is run at the Everest Marathon in Nepal, which starts at Gorak Shep at 5,184 meters (17,000 ft) and finishes in Namche Bazaar at 3,446 meters.
The world record for the longest continuous single-player video game session is 135 hours, set by Carrie Swidecki of the USA playing Just Dance in 2015.

The world's most successful intelligence agency by number of documented coups and regime changes is the CIA, which has been credibly linked to interventions in more than 50 countries since its founding in 1947.
The world's longest recorded echo is 75 seconds, recorded in an empty oil storage tank in Inchindown, Scotland, which has a reverberation time that makes it the most reverberant space ever measured.
The record for the most simultaneous chess games played is 604, by Grandmaster Susan Polgar of Hungary/USA in 2005, who won 590, drew 7, and lost 7.
The most expensive car ever sold at auction is the 1955 Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupé, which sold at a private auction for €135 million ($142 million) in May 2022.
The record for the farthest distance a golf ball has been driven by a robot is 517.6 yards (473.3 meters), achieved by the LDRIC robot built by Golf Laboratories in 2019.
The world's fastest human in water (100m backstroke) is Ryan Murphy of the USA who set the world record of 51.85 seconds at the 2016 Olympic Games in Rio de Janeiro.

The world's most luminous galaxy is W2246-0526, a 'hot DOG' (Hot Dust-Obscured Galaxy), which was discovered in 2015 and emits light equivalent to more than 300 trillion suns—the brightest known galaxy.
The world's most massive single crystal ever grown is a 120 kg sapphire boule produced by the Saint-Gobain company in France for scientific and industrial optical uses.

The world's longest confirmed lineage of a single family claiming continuous royal descent is the Japanese Imperial Family, with Emperor Naruhito representing the 126th generation of an unbroken dynasty dating back over 2,600 years.
The world's largest recorded great white shark was 6.1 meters (20 ft) long and was called 'Deep Blue,' spotted off the coast of Guadalupe Island, Mexico and later near Hawaii in 2019.
The most runs scored in Test cricket history by one batter is 15,921, by Sachin Tendulkar of India over 200 Test matches between 1989 and 2013.
The world's longest confirmed migration by a land mammal is that of caribou (reindeer) herds in northern Canada, which can travel up to 5,000 km annually—the longest land migration of any mammal.

The highest-scoring NBA season in history by average points per game across the entire league was the 1961–62 season, when teams averaged 118.8 points per game, driven largely by Wilt Chamberlain's unprecedented dominance.
The world's highest measured wind gust ever recorded at a surface station is 408 km/h (253 mph) at Barrow Island, Western Australia on April 10, 1996, during Tropical Cyclone Olivia.
The most copies of a single newspaper edition ever printed was 13 million for the London Daily Mirror on May 9, 1945, celebrating VE Day—the end of World War II in Europe.

The most accurate clock in existence is a strontium atomic lattice clock at NIST in Boulder, Colorado, which would neither gain nor lose a second in over 15 billion years—longer than the age of the universe.

source.name: National Institute of Standards and Technology

text: The world's most successful Formula E driver is António Félix da Costa of Portugal, who won the 2019–20 Formula E championship with Techeetah and holds multiple race wins in the all-electric motorsport series.
The world's most northerly permanently inhabited settlement is Alert, Nunavut, Canada, located at 82°28'N latitude—only 817 km from the North Pole.
The world's most southerly permanently inhabited settlement is Puerto Williams in Tierra del Fuego, Chile, with a population of about 2,500 located at 54°56'S latitude.
The fastest circumnavigation of Earth by car (land and sea) is 5 days, 15 hours, 25 minutes, completed by Arvid Hennig and his team in 2006, driving and ferrying across continents.
The most successive football (soccer) World Cups attended by a referee is 5, achieved by Ángel Néstor Coerezza of Argentina, who officiated at World Cups from 1990 to 2006.
The world's largest collection of snow globes belongs to Wendy Suen of Hong Kong, who has amassed over 4,059 snow globes as of 2016, recognised by Guinness World Records.
The world's longest confirmed snake ever recorded is a reticulated python measured at 7.67 meters (25 ft 2 in), named Fluffy, which was kept at the Columbus Zoo in Ohio, USA.
The world's greatest known tidal range is found in the Bay of Fundy in Nova Scotia, Canada, where tides can vary up to 16.3 meters (53.5 ft) between high and low tide.
The record for the most YouTube subscribers for an individual creator (non-corporate) is held by MrBeast (Jimmy Donaldson), who surpassed 200 million subscribers in 2023.
The largest nuclear explosion ever detonated was the Soviet Tsar Bomba on October 30, 1961, at 50 megatons of TNT-equivalent yield—about 3,800 times the power of the Hiroshima bomb.
The most expensive musical recording ever sold is a single acetate disc of 'Good Luck Charm' by Elvis Presley, which fetched £292,000 ($405,000) at Omega Auctions in 2016.

The world's largest beaver dam, detectable by satellite, is located in Wood Buffalo National Park, Alberta, Canada, measuring approximately 850 meters in length—almost twice the length of the Hoover Dam.
The world record for the highest number of satellite launches on a single rocket is 143 satellites, aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket on the Transporter-1 mission in January 2021.
The most popular theme park worldwide by annual attendance is the Magic Kingdom at Walt Disney World Resort in Orlando, Florida, which typically receives over 20 million visitors annually.
The world's largest annual fireworks display by number of shells is the National Day celebration in Abu Dhabi, UAE, which set a Guinness record in 2011 with 77,282 firework shells fired in 6 minutes.
The world's largest underground lake is Dragon's Breath Cave lake in Namibia, with a surface area of 2.61 hectares at 60 meters underground, discovered in 1986.
The world's fastest typing speed on a keyboard is 212 words per minute, achieved by Barbara Blackburn of the USA using a Dvorak keyboard layout in 2005.

The record for the most touchdowns received in an NFL career is 197, by Jerry Rice of the San Francisco 49ers, who also holds the records for most career receptions (1,549) and receiving yards (22,895).
The most expensive lunch box ever sold at auction is one belonging to The Beatles from 1965, which fetched $39,200 at Christie's New York in 2009.

The world's fastest ever submarine (nuclear-powered) is the Soviet K-222 (also known as Papa-class), which reached 44.7 knots (82.8 km/h) in 1968 during sea trials—still the fastest submarine on record.
The world's most successful Olympic sport country per capita is Jamaica in sprinting, having won more short-sprint Olympic medals than any country relative to its population of 3 million.
The world's most powerful rocket ever launched successfully was the Saturn V, standing 110.6 meters tall and developing 34,020 kN of thrust at launch, used by NASA's Apollo and Skylab programs.
The world's largest wave pool is the Siam Park wave pool in Tenerife, Spain, which creates waves up to 3 meters (10 ft) high in a 6,500 m² lagoon, holding over 6,000 guests.
The most expensive painting sold by a living artist at auction is 'Rabbit' by Jeff Koons, which sold at Christie's New York in May 2019 for $91.075 million.
The world's highest-elevation city with over one million people is Bogotá, Colombia, at 2,600 meters (8,530 ft) above sea level, with a population of over 7 million.
The most aces served in a single Wimbledon gentlemen's singles match is 113, by John Isner of the USA vs. Nicolas Mahut of France in 70-68 final set on June 23–25, 2010.

source.name: The All England Lawn Tennis Club

text: The world's longest tennis match in history was 11 hours 5 minutes, played between John Isner and Nicolas Mahut at Wimbledon 2010, with the final set ending 70–68.
The world's fastest ocean crossing by a sailing yacht was achieved by the IDEC Sport trimaran, which sailed 4,714 nautical miles (8,730 km) across the Atlantic in 5 days 14 hours 21 minutes in 2018.
The world's smallest dog by height on record is Miracle Milly, a Chihuahua from Puerto Rico who measured 9.65 cm (3.8 in) tall, confirmed by Guinness World Records in 2013.
The world's tallest horse ever was Sampson (later renamed Mammoth), a Shire horse foaled in 1846 in England who stood 2.19 meters (86.5 in) at the shoulder.

The world's most powerful earthquake in terms of seismic energy released was the 1960 Valdivia earthquake in Chile at magnitude 9.5 (Mw), which released roughly twice the seismic energy of the second-most powerful on record.

The world record for longest distance covered by a solar-powered boat across an ocean is the transatlantic journey of PlanetSolar, which completed the first solar circumnavigation of the globe in May 2012 over 584 days.
The largest lake by surface area is the Caspian Sea, which despite its name is a fully enclosed saline lake covering 371,000 km² bordered by Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran, and Azerbaijan.
The most points ever scored in a single ATP Tour tennis match is 502, during the Isner-Mahut match at Wimbledon 2010, which included 218 games and took 11 hours 5 minutes.
The world's largest privately funded scientific project is ITER, the international fusion reactor experiment in France, with a total project cost estimated at over €20 billion involving 35 nations.

The most expensive single item ever insured is the 'Madonna with the Yarnwinder' painting by Leonardo da Vinci, insured for an undisclosed amount said to exceed $300 million during its transportation between collections.

The world's deepest pool is the Blue Abyss facility in Colchester, UK (under development), designed at 50 meters; the current record is held by Y-40 Deep Joy in Italy at 42.15 meters (138.3 ft) depth.
The world's longest golf course is the International Golf Club in Bolton, Massachusetts, with a total course length of 8,325 yards (7,612 m) from the back tees.
The most expensive spiders kept in captivity for venom extraction are the Sydney funnel-web spiders, whose antivenom from venom milking has saved hundreds of lives in Australia since 1981.

The world's first and oldest still-active lighthouse is the Tower of Hercules in La Coruña, Spain, a Roman-era lighthouse built in the 1st century AD, still guiding ships today after over 1,900 years.
The most passes completed in a single NFL game is 45 by Drew Brees of the New Orleans Saints during a 2016 regular season game, part of his record-setting career completion percentage.
The most expensive pair of shoes ever sold are Dorothy's Ruby Slippers from The Wizard of Oz (1939), which fetched $2 million at Heritage Auctions in 2023.
The world record for highest altitude base jump from a fixed object was made from 6,604 meters (21,666 ft) at Meru Peak in India by Miles Daisher and Craig Jones in 2006.
The most NFL Super Bowl titles won by a single franchise is 7, by the New England Patriots (6) and the Kansas City Chiefs—although as of 2024, Kansas City Chiefs are at 4 and Patriots at 6.
The world's largest mangrove forest is the Sundarbans, a transboundary mangrove area shared by Bangladesh and India, covering 10,000 km² and home to the Bengal tiger.

The world record for the longest video game development is Star Citizen by Cloud Imperium Games, which entered production in 2012 and had raised over $700 million in crowdfunding by 2024 without a full release.
The most expensive violin ever sold was a 1741 Guarneri del Gesù, the 'Vieuxtemps' violin, valued at approximately $16 million when sold to a private collector in 2012.
The world's largest freshwater fish by weight is the giant freshwater stingray (Urogymnus polylepis) of Southeast Asia; one caught in Cambodia in 2022 weighed 300 kg (661 lbs).
The world's highest rate of annual lightning strikes recorded at a single weather station is at the Maracaibo Beacon in Venezuela, which averages 233 strikes per square kilometer per year.

source.name: Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society

text: The world record for the highest mountain biking speed on snow is 227.72 km/h (141.5 mph), achieved by Éric Barone of France at the Cerro Negro volcano in Nicaragua in 2017.
The most expensive painting by a woman artist sold at auction is Georgia O'Keeffe's 'Jimson Weed/White Flower No. 1,' which sold at Sotheby's New York in November 2014 for $44.4 million.
The most medals won by a single country in a Summer Olympics in the modern era (post-1988) is 130, by the United States at the 2004 Athens Olympics.
The most people simultaneously performing the same magic trick is 256, achieved by magicians in Hungary in 2012 who all performed card tricks at the same moment.
The world's most volcanically active region on Earth's surface is Iceland, where the country sits on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and averages one volcanic eruption every 3 to 5 years.
The most theatrical performances in a single production run is 6,680, achieved by The Phantom of the Opera on Broadway from January 26, 1988, to April 16, 2023—35 years of consecutive performances.
The world's longest confirmed chain of human handholding was Hands Across America on May 25, 1986, where approximately 6.5 million people formed a human chain across the continental USA.

The largest diamond ever cut from a raw diamond is the Great Star of Africa (Cullinan I), weighing 530.4 carats, cut from the 3,106.75-carat Cullinan Diamond and set in the head of the British Sovereign's Sceptre.

The world's fastest supercomputer measured by LINPACK performance as of 2024 is Frontier at Oak Ridge National Lab, but China's Sunway TaihuLight (2016) was notable for using entirely domestically-made processors.

The largest meteorite from Mars found on Earth is the Tissint meteorite, which fell in Morocco in July 2011; another Martian meteorite, ALH84001, famously showed possible signs of ancient microbial life in 1996.

source.name: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History

text: The world's most visited website in 2023 was Google.com, with approximately 85 billion monthly visits, followed by YouTube at 34 billion and Facebook at 20 billion.
The world's most expensive military aircraft is the B-21 Raider strategic bomber, estimated at $692 million per unit, which made its debut flight in November 2023 for the US Air Force.
The world record for the most trees planted in a single day by one person is 15,170, achieved by Ken Chaplin in Saskatchewan, Canada, in 2001.
The world's most powerful commercial nuclear reactor by output is the 1,600 MW EPR at the Flamanville Nuclear Power Plant in France, which entered commercial operation in 2024.
The most successful country in the history of the Rugby World Cup by number of titles is New Zealand, with 4 championships (1987, 2011, 2015, 2023).

The world's most expensive tea is Da-Hong Pao rock oolong from China's Wuyi Mountains, where the original six ancient tea bushes are protected by the Chinese government; auction prices have reached $1.4 million per kilogram.
The world's oldest known living clonal plant colony is Old Tjikko, a Norway Spruce in Sweden whose root system was carbon-dated to 9,550 years ago, making it one of the oldest living organisms.
The most international caps (appearances) in women's soccer history is 218, held by Kristine Lilly of the USA, who played for the US Women's National Team from 1987 to 2010.
The world's largest impact crater still on Earth's surface is the Vredefort Crater in South Africa, approximately 300 km in diameter, formed by an asteroid impact about 2 billion years ago.
The world record for continuous laughter is 3 hours and 6 minutes, achieved by Barry Kirk at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe in 2008.

The world's most accurate map ever made is NASA's Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) dataset from 2000, which mapped 80% of Earth's land surface with a resolution of 30 meters using synthetic-aperture radar.

The most expensive dress ever auctioned is the 'Happy Birthday, Mr. President' gown worn by Marilyn Monroe in 1962 when she sang to John F. Kennedy, which sold for $4.8 million at Ripley's Believe It or Not in 2016.
The tallest person alive today (as of 2024) is Sultan Kösen of Turkey, who measures 2.51 meters (8 ft 2.8 in) and also holds the record for the largest hands of a living person.

The world's most powerful radio telescope is the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical Telescope (FAST) in Guizhou, China, with a collecting area of 195,000 m²—more than twice the size of the Arecibo Observatory it surpassed.

The world's most endangered large mammal is the Javan rhinoceros, with only about 70 individuals remaining in Ujung Kulon National Park in Indonesia—making it the most critically endangered rhinoceros species.

The record for the highest number of paintings sold by one artist in their lifetime is approximately 60,000–75,000, attributed to Picasso, who also holds the world record for most expensive painting sold at auction for a 20th-century artist.
The world's oldest living marine mammal is a bowhead whale estimated to be approximately 211 years old, identified by harpoon fragments and genomic sequencing, still alive as of recent surveys.
The most successful Paralympic athlete of all time by total gold medals is Trischa Zorn of the USA, who won 55 gold medals in swimming across seven Paralympic Games from 1980 to 2004.
The world record for the most pushups in 24 hours is 46,001, achieved by Charles Servizio of the USA on April 24–25, 1993.
The world's most frequently reproduced painting is The Starry Night by Vincent van Gogh, with an estimated 250 million+ reproductions sold globally, including posters, prints, and merchandise.
The farthest humans have sent a probe is Voyager 1, launched in 1977, which as of 2024 is over 24 billion km from Earth—more than 160 times the Earth-Sun distance—in interstellar space.
The most consecutive appearances in the NBA Finals is 10, by the Boston Celtics, who appeared in 10 consecutive Finals from 1957 to 1966 and won 8 in a row.
The world's highest paid athlete in a single year (all sports combined) was Cristiano Ronaldo in 2023, earning approximately $136 million including salary, bonuses, and endorsements.

The world's largest desert in terms of area (including cold deserts) that receives the least annual rainfall is the Dry Valleys of Antarctica, parts of which have not received rain in approximately 2 million years.
The most expensive item ever sold on eBay was a Gigayacht (a private 405-foot luxury superyacht), listed at $168 million in 2006—though the final sale is unverified.
The record for the most distance covered running backwards in 24 hours is 153.52 km (95.4 miles), achieved by Achim Aretz of Germany at an indoor track in 2004.
The world's most expensive board game sold at auction is a 1933 Charles Darrow original Monopoly set handmade by the inventor himself, which sold for $146,500 at Sotheby's in 2011.
The world's largest spider web was discovered in Texas in 2007, when an unusual social species of spiders cooperated to create a web stretching 180 meters (600 ft) in a state park.

The most goals scored in a professional ice hockey career (all leagues) is estimated at over 1,000, a milestone first reached by Wayne Gretzky; his 894 NHL goals remain the most in the league's history.
The record for the most people simultneously solving a Rubik's Cube is 3,248, set during a competition in Hong Kong in 2012, each person solving a cube at the same time.
The world's most visited building per year is the Vatican Museums complex, which received nearly 7 million visitors in 2023, making it the most visited museum/monument in Italy.
The most expensive domain name ever sold is sex.com, which was acquired by Escom LLC in 2010 for approximately $13 million, making it the highest-priced domain name sale in internet history.
The world's largest emerald ever found is the Teodora Emerald, weighing 57,500 carats (11.5 kg), discovered in Brazil in 2001 and currently held at auction.
The record for the fastest completion of a 1,000-piece jigsaw puzzle is 1 hour 5 minutes 9 seconds, achieved by Thomas Wellmann of Germany in 2022.
The world record for the most national Olympic gold medals at a single Games by an athlete from a developing nation is 4, achieved by multiple African athletes in athletics at various Olympics.

The world's most aggressive invasive species is the brown tree snake (Boiga irregularis), which has driven 9 of Guam's 12 native forest bird species to extinction since its accidental introduction around 1950.
The world's most prolific songwriter is credited to be Paul McCartney, who has written or co-written 32 No. 1 hit singles in the UK and USA—the most commercially successful songwriter in history.

The world record for the longest time someone has waited for a concert ticket is over 7 years; Londoner Linda Tennant began sleeping outside the Hammersmith Odeon in 1980 for Led Zeppelin, who never played there again.

The world's most visited country is France, which welcomed approximately 100 million international tourists in 2023, making it the world's most-visited tourist destination for the 7th consecutive year.
The world's deepest shipwreck discovered is the USS Johnston, a Fletcher-class destroyer sunk during the Battle of Leyte Gulf in 1944, found by Victor Vescovo at 6,469 meters depth in 2021.
The most consecutive days of above-average global temperatures on record occurred in 2023, when Earth experienced 12 consecutive months of record-breaking heat from July 2023 to June 2024.
The world's most copied artwork in history is the Mona Lisa by Leonardo da Vinci, painted between 1503 and 1519; it is the most recognized and most written-about painting in the world.
The world's largest confirmed tornado by damage path length was the Tri-State Tornado of March 18, 1925, which traveled 352 km (219 miles) across Missouri, Illinois, and Indiana, killing 695 people.
The world's longest commercial railway line is the Trans-Siberian Railway, running 9,289 km (5,772 miles) from Moscow to Vladivostok, crossing 8 time zones and taking about 7 days to traverse.
The most successful rowing nation in Olympic history is Great Britain, which has won more rowing gold medals at the Olympics than any other country, with 30 gold medals from 1900 to 2020.
The world record for the fastest 200m sprint is 19.19 seconds, set by Usain Bolt of Jamaica at the 2009 World Athletics Championships in Berlin—the same event where he broke the 100m record.
The world's fastest commercial internet speeds are found in Singapore, where a national average internet connection speed of 290 Mbps was recorded in 2023—the fastest national average in the world.
The world's oldest known written legal code is the Code of Ur-Nammu, enacted around 2100–2050 BCE in ancient Sumer (modern Iraq), predating the more famous Code of Hammurabi by 300 years.
The highest vertical-drop ski run in the world is the Harakiri run in Mayrhofen, Austria, with a maximum gradient of 78%—steep enough that most recreational skiers cannot stop without falling.
The world record for the most donuts eaten in 3 minutes is 6, a record held in competitive eating circuits—though the Nathan's Famous contest remains the most famous eating competition in the world.
The most appearances in a FIFA World Cup as a player (most caps) is 26, held by Lothar Matthäus of West Germany/Germany across five World Cups from 1982 to 1998.

The world's most isolated person in recorded history was Michael Collins, Command Module Pilot of Apollo 11, who orbited the Moon completely alone for 21 minutes while Armstrong and Aldrin walked on the lunar surface.

The largest confirmed volcanic eruption in recorded history by ash volume was the 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora in Indonesia, which released 160 km³ of ash and caused the 'Year Without a Summer' in 1816.
The world record for the most miles driven in an electric vehicle on a single charge is 1,608 miles (2,587 km), set by a modified Mercedes Vision EQXX prototype in 2023.
The most successful club in FIFA Club World Cup history is Real Madrid, who have won the tournament 8 times between 2014 and 2023.
The world's largest amphitheater still standing is the Roman Colosseum in Rome, built between 70–80 AD, with a seating capacity of up to 80,000 spectators in its prime.
The world's tallest sand castle ever built reached 21.16 meters (69.4 ft), constructed by a team in Binz, Germany in 2019.
The most matches won in a single Wimbledon career is 105, by Roger Federer of Switzerland, who won the tournament eight times and played from 1999 to 2021.

source.name: The All England Lawn Tennis Club

text: The world's largest natural gas reserve belongs to Russia, which holds approximately 37.4 trillion cubic meters (2023 estimate), representing about 19% of the world's total proven reserves.

The largest collection of meteorites owned by a single private individual is held by Darryl Pitt of the USA, who has curated a collection of over 400 meteorites including fragments from Mars, the Moon, and major falls.

The world's longest underwater cave system is Sistema Sac Actun in Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula, with over 368 km (229 miles) of mapped passages, confirmed in 2018 after the merging of two separate cave systems.
The world record for the highest combined score in a single snowboard halfpipe competition run is 100, achieved by Shaun White of the USA at the 2012 Winter X Games in Aspen, Colorado.
The world record for the most socks worn simultaneously on one foot is 267, achieved by Faisal Al Hammadi of the UAE in 2020, each sock applied individually.
The most expensive chocolate ever made is 'The H.O.F', or 'House of Fabrice' chocolate bar by DeLafée of Switzerland, which contains edible 24-carat gold flakes and sells for up to $500 per bar.

The world's largest beaver in recorded fossil history is Castoroides ohioensis, an extinct giant beaver of North America that could reach 2.5 meters long and weigh 100 kg, living until about 10,000 years ago.

source.name: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History

text: The world record for the most words per minute spoken on radio was 655 wpm, achieved by Canadian sports broadcaster Fran Capo in 1986, verified by Guinness World Records.
The world's longest suspension footbridge is the Highline 179 near Reutte, Austria, spanning 406 meters at 114 meters above the Fernpass and completed in 2015.
The most expensive truffle ever sold was a white Alba truffle weighing 1.51 kg (3.3 lbs), sold for $160,406 at the Grinzing auction in Vienna in 2007 to a casino owner from Macau.
The world's oldest piece of music ever performed from notation is the Seikilos Epitaph, a Greek song carved on a grave stele from around 200 BCE, discovered in Aydin, Turkey in 1883.
The most cricket World Cup (ODI) wins by a team is 5, by Australia (1987, 1999, 2003, 2007, 2023), making the Australians the most successful team in the history of the ICC Cricket World Cup.
The world's largest gold reserve held by a central bank is the United States Federal Reserve, which holds approximately 8,133 tonnes—about 26% of all government-held gold in the world.
The world's largest confirmed reservoir of oil is the Ghawar Field in Saudi Arabia, containing an estimated 80 billion barrels of proven reserves and producing about 3.8 million barrels per day.
The world's fastest speed reached by a human in a wind tunnel is 617 km/h (383 mph), achieved by Henrik Raimer of Sweden in the indoor skydiving world championships.
The world record for the largest serving of fish and chips (single portion) is 36 kg (79.37 lbs), prepared by restaurateurs in Cape Town, South Africa in 2016.
The world's most successful marathon nation is Kenya, whose runners have dominated major world marathons; Kenyan athletes have won the Boston Marathon men's race 39 times between 1988 and 2023.
The world's highest-altitude airport in regular commercial use is Daocheng Yading Airport in Sichuan, China, at 4,411 meters (14,472 ft) above sea level, opened in 2013.

The world's most visited country per capita (ratio of tourists to residents) is Andorra, a microstate in the Pyrenees that receives approximately 8 million visitors annually against a resident population of just 77,000.
The most consecutive days without food survived by a human is 382 days, by Angus Barbieri of Dundee, Scotland, who fasted under medical supervision from June 1965 to July 1966, losing 125 kg.
The world's oldest extant manuscript library is the Monastery of Saint Catherine at the foot of Mount Sinai in Egypt, which has preserved papyri and early Christian texts since the 4th century AD.
The world record for the highest number of languages in which a person's voice has been heard simultaneously is 41 languages, during a United Nations live translation session in 2019.
The world's highest-producing dairy cow in recorded history was a Holstein cow named 'Ever-Green-View My 1326-ET', which produced 32,804 kg (72,321 lbs) of milk in 365 days in 2016 in Wisconsin, USA.
The world record for the longest single-engine airplane flight is 7,671 km (4,766 miles), flown by a Cessna 172 modified by Vern Durrance in 1958 using a special fuel system.

The world's most expensive car produced in limited series is the Rolls-Royce Boat Tail, with three bespoke commissions each priced at approximately $28 million—the most expensive new car ever commissioned.
The most laps completed in the Le Mans 24-hour race is 397, achieved by Porsche 919 Hybrid driven by Timo Bernhard, Brendon Hartley, and Mark Webber in 2015.
The world's most successful Dakar Rally competitor by wins is Stéphane Peterhansel of France, nicknamed 'Monsieur Dakar', who has won the rally 14 times across motorcycle and car categories.

The world's most powerful earthquake of the 21st century was the 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake off the coast of Sumatra, magnitude 9.1–9.3 (Mw), which triggered the deadliest tsunami in history killing over 230,000 people.
The world's most frequently performed opera is La Traviata by Giuseppe Verdi, with an estimated 150+ performances per year globally in major opera houses, making it the most staged opera in history.
The world's largest living bird by height is the ostrich (Struthio camelus), which can reach 2.8 meters (9.2 ft) in height and weigh up to 156 kg (344 lbs).

The most number of countries visited by a commercial flight on a single ticket route is 28, as part of a round-the-world fare offered by several airline alliances including Oneworld and Star Alliance.
The world's most crowded country by population density (excluding microstates and city-states) is Bangladesh, with approximately 1,265 people per square kilometer across its 130,000 km² territory.
The world's largest ocean garbage patch is the Great Pacific Garbage Patch, spanning an estimated 1.6 million km² between Hawaii and California and containing roughly 80,000 tonnes of plastic debris.
The most wins at the Crossfit Games (overall individual) is 4 consecutive titles, won by Mat Fraser of the USA from 2016 to 2020, who is considered the greatest CrossFit athlete of all time.

The world's highest sustained wind on Earth (annual average) is at Mount Washington, New Hampshire, USA, which averages 56.3 km/h (35 mph) annually and held the world's wind gust record from 1934 until 1996.
The most successful short-track speed skater in Olympic history is Viktor Ahn (formerly Ahn Hyun-soo) who won 8 Olympic medals (6 gold, 2 bronze) competing for South Korea and Russia.
The world's largest diamond deposit (by value) is the Argyle Diamond Mine in Western Australia, which produced 90% of the world's pink and red diamonds before closing in 2020.
The record for the most career PGA Tour wins is 82, by Sam Snead of the USA across his career from 1936 to 1965—a record that held until 2021 when Tiger Woods matched it.

The world's most luminous known natural object is a quasar named J0529-4351, discovered in 2024, which shines with the brightness of 500 trillion suns—powered by the fastest-growing black hole ever found.
The most Olympic track cycling gold medals won is 8, by Chris Hoy of Great Britain who competed from 2000 to 2012 and is the most successful track cyclist in Olympic history.
The world's smallest country by total area is Vatican City (0.44 km²), while the next smallest are Monaco (2.02 km²), San Marino (61 km²), Liechtenstein (160 km²), and Malta (316 km²).
The most expensive photograph ever auctioned (as of 2023) is Cindy Sherman's 'Untitled #96' which sold at Christie's New York in May 2011 for $3.89 million.
The world record for the most consecutive basketball free throws without a miss is 5,221, by Ted St. Martin of Jacksonville, Florida, set in 1996.

The world's largest naturally occurring crystals are in the Cave of the Crystals (Cueva de los Cristales) in Chihuahua, Mexico, where selenite crystals reach 12 meters (39 ft) in length and weigh up to 55 tonnes.
The most widely used messaging application in history is WhatsApp, with over 2 billion monthly active users in 2024, transmitting over 100 billion messages per day.

The record for the most languages in which a song has been officially released is 36, by 'Counting Stars' by OneRepublic, which was released with official video translations into 36 languages by YouTube in 2013.
The world's longest known migration of any fish is that of the European eel (Anguilla anguilla), which travels up to 6,000 km from European rivers to spawn in the Sargasso Sea near Bermuda.
The world's largest confirmed dinosaur by weight was Patagotitan mayorum, a titanosaur sauropod from Argentina estimated at up to 76 tonnes and 40 meters (131 ft) in length.

source.name: Proceedings of the Royal Society B

text: The most goals scored in the Champions League/European Cup in a single season is 17, by Cristiano Ronaldo for Real Madrid in the 2013–14 season.
The world record for the most jumps performed by a horse in a single day is 2,017, set by Camille Judet riding a horse named Lazkao Txiki in France in 2009.
The world's longest confirmed natural salt cave system is Malham Cave in Mount Sodom, Israel, with over 10 km of passages cut by rainwater dissolving salt rock underground.
The fastest completion of a 4×100m relay in Olympic history is 36.84 seconds, set by Jamaica (Nesta Carter, Michael Frater, Yohan Blake, Usain Bolt) at the 2012 London Olympics.
The world's most expensive private school is Institut auf dem Rosenberg in St. Gallen, Switzerland, with annual fees exceeding CHF 150,000 ($165,000) per year.
The largest known structure in the observable universe is the Hercules-Corona Borealis Great Wall, a vast galaxy filament approximately 10 billion light-years across, reported in 2013.
The world's largest collection of teddy bears belongs to Jackie Miley of the USA, who has amassed over 8,026 teddy bears as of 2011, housed in a dedicated museum in Hill City, South Dakota.
The world's smallest country to ever win a soccer World Cup group stage game is Iceland, with a population of 334,000, which defeated Austria 2–1 at UEFA Euro 2016 in its first major tournament.
The world's largest indoor garden is the Gardens by the Bay in Singapore, with three interconnected domed conservatories—the Flower Dome (1.28 hectares) is the world's largest glass greenhouse.
The most wickets taken in Women's Test cricket career is 77, by Mary Duggan of England, who played from 1949 to 1963.
The world's fastest time to climb El Capitan (Nose route) is 1 hour 58 minutes 7 seconds, set by Tommy Caldwell and Alex Honnold in June 2018, more than halving the previous record.
The world's largest natural reservoir of fresh water is the Antarctic ice sheet, which holds approximately 26.5 million km³ of water—about 70% of all fresh water on Earth.

The world's longest recorded lightning bolt measured 768 km (477 miles) in a single stroke across parts of the southern United States in April 2020, confirmed by the World Meteorological Organization.
The most hat-tricks scored in a single FIFA World Cup finals tournament is 3, achieved by Grzegorz Lato of Poland at the 1974 World Cup in West Germany, where he also won the Golden Boot.
The world's largest coral atoll by land area is Kiritimati (Christmas Island) in Kiribati, covering 388 km² with a massive lagoon, the largest atoll in the world.
The world's most successful Winter Olympic country by total medals all-time is Norway, with 405 Winter Olympic medals (148 gold) as of 2022—more than any other nation in Winter Olympics history.
The world record for the most marathons run in a single year is 365, completing one marathon per day for an entire year, achieved by Stefaan Engels of Belgium in 2011.
The world's rarest blood type is Rh-null, sometimes called 'golden blood,' which has no antigens on the red blood cell surface; fewer than 50 people worldwide are known to have this blood type.

source.name: International Journal of Blood Transfusion and Immunohematology

text: The world record for highest number of simultaneous parachute jumps is 400, performed by members of the US Army Golden Knights parachute team and civilians during a 2006 event in Arizona.
The world's fastest completion of Mount Everest ascent from base camp is 8 hours 25 minutes, accomplished by Lakpa Gelu Sherpa of Nepal in 2003 on the standard South Col route.

The world's heaviest fruit ever grown is a pumpkin weighing 1,226.9 kg (2,703.9 lbs), grown by Travis Gienger of the USA in 2023; the heaviest watermelon weighed 159 kg (350.5 lbs) grown by Chris Kent in 2013.
The world's most species-rich country by number of documented species is Brazil, with over 116,000 known animal and plant species—the highest biodiversity of any country on Earth.

The world's most expensive commercial art theft in history was the 1990 Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum heist in Boston, where 13 artworks valued at approximately $500 million were stolen and have never been recovered.
The most accurate measurement of a fundamental physical constant is the value of the electron's magnetic moment, measured to 13 significant figures—the most precisely measured quantity in physics.
The world record for the heaviest egg laid by a living bird belongs to an ostrich egg weighing 2.589 kg (5 lbs 11.36 oz), laid at a farm in Sweden in 2008.

The world's most efficient solar cell ever measured in a laboratory setting achieved 47.6% energy conversion efficiency, demonstrated by researchers at the National Renewable Energy Laboratory in the USA in 2022.

The world's fastest land animal over long distances is the pronghorn antelope of North America, which can sustain speeds of 88 km/h (55 mph) for miles and can outrun almost any predator over distance.
The world's tallest tree species is the coast redwood (Sequoia sempervirens); the tallest known individual, named Hyperion, stands 115.92 meters (380.3 ft) in Redwood National Park, California.
The most touchdowns thrown in a single NFL season is 55, by Peyton Manning of the Denver Broncos in 2013, breaking Tom Brady's then-record of 50 set in 2007.

The world's largest ancient pyramid by volume is the Great Pyramid of Cholula (Tlachihualtepetl) in Puebla, Mexico, containing approximately 4.45 million cubic meters—nearly 4 times the volume of the Great Pyramid of Giza.
The world's most successful Olympic shooting nation is the United States, which has won 115 Olympic medals in shooting sports across the Summer Games, more than any other country.

The world's most biodiverse marine environment per unit area is the Coral Triangle—covering the Philippines, Indonesia, Malaysia, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, and Timor-Leste—which is home to 76% of all known coral species and 37% of all reef fish.
